Our team is sharp, motivated, and deeply committed to Rogo’s mission. We take ownership of complex problems and stay relentlessly focused on our users. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, demand excellence, and want to help build the future of finance, we invite you to join us.

About the Role 

As a Solutions Architect, you will guide mid-market financial institutions through adopting Rogo’s AI platform. You will translate business and technical requirements into secure, scalable solutions that integrate with customers’ existing systems and workflows.

You will combine deep cloud architecture knowledge, practical software engineering and strong customer ownership. Working across technical evaluation, implementation and ongoing adoption, you will partner with customer teams and Rogo’s Sales, Customer Success, Product and Engineering teams to deliver successful outcomes.

What You Will Own 

Customer collaboration

- Act as a trusted advisor to customers, deeply understanding their business challenges and technical requirements.

- Lead architectural discussions and technical evaluations, using established approaches and drawing on experienced colleagues for more complex requirements.

- Build and maintain strong relationships with customer business and technical teams to ensure successful deployments and long-term satisfaction.

title: Senior Applied AI Engineer, Document Intelligence
description:
Headquarters: New Jersey, USA

URL: https://vertican.com 

About the role

For 40 years Vertican has buildt software that runs law firms. One year ago we created a new modern AI platform for document automation (processing/extraction/redacting) which our customers have been adopting faster than any product we've ever had. Our suite of AI-enabled products save customers thousands of hours each week by processing high volumes of documents with precision and speed.The AI team is growing and we'd like you to join.

We are hiring an engineer to own the document processing pipelines end to end: design, benchmarking, experimenting with new architectures and tools, threshold required for deploying a new pipeline, etc.

We believe it's important to build our own tooling to help us run, improve, and measure our applications. Therefore, the ideal candidate thinks outside the box on how to not just build the product/pipeline, but also the tooling needed around it.

You will be the first dedicated ML hire on the product taking over from the engineering manager who build the current solution and will work directly with the founding engineering team.

This is a senior, hands-on individual-contributor role, but we are small team and you'll be involved in design, planning, roadmapping, and architectural decisions.

What you will do

Design the pipelines. Own the architecture of the extraction-to-posting pipelines: page classification, field extraction, candidate retrieval, claim matching, confidence gating and the hand-off to human review, etc. Decide where rules end and models begin, and what each stage must guarantee to the next, what the separation of concerns are, etc.

We have different pipelines for different document types and expect that at any given point in time we may have new ones emerge and may consolidate others.

Evaluate new systems before we adopt them. Run structured trials of candidate components and recommend what to keep. Examples include probabilistic record linkage (Splink), Azure AI Content Understanding and Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI and Foundry-hosted models, and LLM agents with tools. Similarly, test new models with the existing pipeline as they are relased from the frontier labs.

Build the evaluation process. You'll own the process of evaluating false positives, false negatives, errors of ommission, etc, that we ultimately use to determine if we should upgrade the pipeline. 

Ship and operate. Take components from trial to production in our python workers on the cloud, instrument them, watch cost and quota, and diagnose the cases reviewers send back.

Set direction. Work with leadereship on the planing for accuracy, cost improvement, and overall product improvements.

What we are looking for

Required 

- 6+ years building ML or data-intensive systems, at least 3 of them owning a production pipeline whose output people acted on.

- Solid backend engineering understanding and ideally cloud architecture understanding.

- Ideally hands-on experience with document understanding: OCR or layout models, field extraction from scanned PDFs, or intelligent document processing products.

- Experience with entity resolution or record linkage at scale (Splink, Dedupe, Zingg, or your own blocking-and-scoring system) against databases of hundreds of thousands of rows.

- You have designed an evaluation from scratch: built a labeled ground-truth set, chosen the metrics, and defended a threshold to a non-technical stakeholder.

- Production experience with LLM APIs, including structured output, tool calling and cost or rate-limit management; you can say when an LLM is the wrong tool.

- Strong Python and SQL. Comfortable reading Postgres query plans and writing the raw query when the ORM gets in the way.

- Engineering/Scientist mindset: you are scientific about testing the pipeline and how results are interpeted/presented.

Nice to have 

- Azure AI services (Content Understanding, Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI, Foundry) or the AWS and GCP equivalents.

- Financial document processing: checks, remittance advices, lockbox files, payment matching, or accounts receivable automation.

- Exposure to collections, legal operations or other regulated workflows handling PII.

- Probabilistic matching theory (Fellegi-Sunter) or active-learning labeling workflows.

- Experience building human-review tooling or feedback loops that feed back into training and evaluation data.

How we work and what we offer

Small team, direct access to large datasets, weekly planning, daily standup, everyone remote in US timezones.

What we offer:

- A small team of tight-knit, like-minded people passionate about high quality software

- Competitive compensation, commensurate with a senior individual-contributor role.

- Monthly payments in USD

Vertican is an equal opportunity employer. We hire on merit and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Modelling & Simulation - Advanced Capabilities
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Advanced Capabilities is the internal warfighter research arm for Anduril's Maneuver Dominance division. We invent new products, inform vehicle specifications, define autonomous tactics, and work out how humans and teams of autonomous systems will operate together in future contested environments.
We're standing up a next generation simulation center in the UAE to run large-scale wargames and experiments with autonomous systems. The on-site team is small and mostly made up of warfighters and analysts. They'll be backed by our engineering teams in the UK and US. 

ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll be the software engineer on the ground. Your main job is to build the models that make our scenarios credible. You'll also own the simulation environment that keeps the center running.
Most of your modelling will be in Python, but you'll also work in our core C++ simulation code when a model needs to go deeper or something breaks. You'll work closely with warfighters to turn their operational questions into working models.

- Build and refine models in Python for sensors, communications, platform movement, weapon effects, electronic warfare, and tactical behaviours, at the level of fidelity the question actually requires

- Install, configure, and maintain the simulation software stack and the compute, networking, and storage it runs on

- Validate new releases before they're used in an exercise, and build automated checks so regressions surface early

- Strong proficiency in Python for modelling, tooling, and automation

- Working proficiency in C++, enough to read, debug, and extend a performance-critical simulation codebase

- Experience building models or simulations of complex systems (agent-based, discrete-event, time-stepped, or similar)

- Comfort with mathematical and physical modelling: dynamics, probability, and stochastic processes

- Military experience, or a genuine interest in the problems warfighters face and how to model them

- Hands-on experience setting up and troubleshooting distributed systems and networks

- Ability to work independently in a small, remote team and communicate clearly with both engineers and operators

- Willingness to relocate to Abu Dhabi

- Eligibility to pass the security and background checks required for sensitive information systems

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Defence, aerospace, or robotics experience, especially mission-level or multi-agent simulation

- Experience with military M&S tools (e.g. AFSIM, VBS, Command PE) or distributed simulation standards (DIS, HLA)

- Experience with large-scale Monte Carlo or design-of-experiments analysis

title: (Junior) Inhouse KI-Spezialist (m/w/d) – Data & Integration
description:
Lkw rollen bei uns schon. Jetzt sollen auch die Daten rollen.

Wir sind die Spedition Diez – ein familiengeführtes Logistikunternehmen am Fuß der Schwäbischen Alb. Bei uns arbeitet schon heute eine KI mit: Claude ist unsere firmeninterne KI. Du bekommst keine fertige IT-Abteilung mit hundert Tickets, sondern eine echte Pionierrolle: Du legst das Fundament für unser Data Warehouse und machst aus verstreuten Daten echtes Wissen für Disposition, Fuhrpark und Geschäftsführung.

Was du bei uns bewegst

- Du baust unser zentrales Data Warehouse von Grund auf auf – Datenmodell, Schnittstellen, Datenqualität.
- Du bindest Soloplan (TMS) und unsere weiteren Systeme an, z. B. Tankkarten- und Mautdaten, Fuhrparkdaten und Buchhaltung.
- Du verbindest Claude mit diesen Daten, z. B. über APIs und MCP-Schnittstellen, damit Fragen wie „Welche Touren waren letzten Monat unrentabel?“ in Sekunden beantwortet sind.
- Du automatisierst Routinearbeiten wie Rechnungsprüfung, Auswertungen und Reports.
- Du bist erste Ansprechperson für KI im Haus: Du schulst Kolleginnen und Kollegen, sammelst Ideen und machst daraus funktionierende Lösungen.
- Du hast Datenschutz und Datensicherheit immer im Blick.
Was du mitbringst

- Ein Studium in Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik, Data Science oder Ähnlichem – oder vergleichbare Erfahrung aus der Praxis.
- Erste praktische Erfahrung mit SQL und mindestens einer Skriptsprache, am liebsten Python.
- Erfahrung mit Schnittstellen (REST-APIs, ETL-Prozesse) und Datenbanken.
- Echte Begeisterung für KI und Large Language Models – und Lust, sie praktisch einzusetzen statt nur darüber zu reden.
- Generalisten-Gen: Du packst gern selbst an, von der Datenbank bis zum Gespräch mit der Disposition.
- Erfahrung in Logistik oder mit Soloplan ist ein Plus, aber kein Muss – auch Berufseinsteiger sind herzlich willkommen, wir geben dir Zeit zum Reinwachsen.
- Gute Deutschkenntnisse.
Was wir dir bieten

- Gestaltungsfreiheit: Du baust etwas Eigenes auf – mit kurzen Wegen direkt zur Geschäftsführung.
- Sichtbare Wirkung: Deine Arbeit verändert spürbar, wie bei uns jeden Tag gearbeitet wird.
- Moderne Werkzeuge: Aktuelle KI-Tools und die Freiheit, Neues auszuprobieren.
- Familiäres Umfeld: Ein bodenständiges Team, flache Hierarchien und ein Du von Anfang an.
- Flexibilität: Flexible Arbeitszeiten.
- Standort mit Lebensqualität: Dettingen unter Teck – gut erreichbar über die A8, zwischen Stuttgart und Alb.
Klingt nach dir?

Dann bewirb dich einfach über JOIN – ein Lebenslauf und ein paar Sätze dazu, warum dich die Stelle reizt, genügen. Zeugnisse können wir gern später nachreichen lassen. Wir freuen uns auf dich!

title: Senior Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
Life at UiPath 

The people at UiPath believe in the transformative power of automation to change how the world works. We’re committed to creating category-leading enterprise software that unleashes that power.

To make that happen, we need people who are curious, self-propelled, generous, and genuine. People who love being part of a fast-moving, fast-thinking growth company. And people who care—about each other, about UiPath, and about our larger purpose.

Could that be you?

Your mission 

As a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer, you will own the delivery of scoped customer implementations and help turn real-world business needs into production-grade agentic automation solutions . You’ll partner closely with customer stakeholders and internal teams to design, build, integrate, and iterate on AI-enabled workflows, balancing speed, reliability, and maintainability. You’ll contribute practical field insights back to the organization, helping refine solution patterns, reusable assets, and implementation playbooks.

Unlike traditional software engineers who build a single product for many customers, FDEs ship tailored solutions directly in customer environments, making the platform real for specific business processes and systems. You’ll operate with increasing independence, drive execution on well-defined workstreams , and collaborate with senior FDEs and product teams to align with broader technical direction. 

What you'll do at UiPath 

- Design and build AI-driven workflows, agents, and automations, aligned with UiPath's architecture and platform standards without requiring regular guidance.

- Build AI Agents using UiPath technologies, including Maestro or Agent Builder

- Apply practical prompt engineering skills to reliably guide agent behavior and understand model tradeoffs (capability, latency, cost) when selecting LLM providers for customer use cases.

- Extend platform functionality using APIs, SDKs, and connectors to address unique customer requirements.

- Debug across systems including AI inference, data pipelines, orchestration layers, and integration points, resolving most issues independently.

- Contribute to internal libraries, reusable components, or frameworks that enhance consistency across customer deployments.

- Anticipate delivery risks and communicate blockers, delays, and scope issues proactively to teammates and stakeholders.

- Use telemetry, insights, and traces to identify optimization opportunities and failure patterns independently.

What you'll bring to the team 

- 5+ years of professional software engineering experience (or equivalent) delivering production software.

- Strong programming skills in Python and/or TypeScript (or similar modern languages).

- Experience building and shipping integrations using APIs and working with cloud services or enterprise systems.

- Comfort operating in customer-facing environments with strong written and verbal communication.

- Ability to independently drive scoped projects, manage risks, and deliver against deadlines.

- Willingness to travel to customer sites as needed.

Our core principles 

- Customer Centric: Stay close to customer users and stakeholders; anchor decisions in outcomes, adoption, and long-term success.

- Breaking Silos: Collaborate across Engineering, Product, Customer Success, and customer teams to unblock delivery and align on the right solution.

- Improving Agility: Prototype, test, ship, observe, and iterate—treat deployments and feedback loops as the fastest way to learn.

- Dealing with Ambiguity: Make progress with incomplete information; clarify requirements through discovery, iteration, and pragmatic tradeoffs.

- Building Focus: Prioritize the highest-impact workstreams, manage scope actively, and deliver durable solutions that customers can run and evolve.

Maybe you don’t tick all the boxes above—but still think you’d be great for the job? Go ahead, apply anyway. Please. Because we know that experience comes in all shapes and sizes—and passion can’t be learned.

Many of our roles allow for flexibility in when and where work gets done. Depending on the needs of the business and the role, the number of hybrid, office-based, and remote workers will vary from team to team. Applications are assessed on a rolling basis and there is no fixed deadline for this requisition. The application window may change depending on the volume of applications received or may close immediately if a qualified candidate is selected.

We value a range of diverse backgrounds, experiences and ideas. We pride ourselves on our diversity and inclusive workplace that provides equal opportunities to all persons regardless of age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, and expression, national origin, disability, neurodiversity, military and/or veteran status, or any other protected classes. Additionally, UiPath provides reasonable accommodations for candidates on request and respects applicants' privacy rights. To review these and other legal disclosures, visit our privacy policy .

title: Member of Technical Staff - Safety
description:
About Black Forest Labs

We're the team behind Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX—foundational technologies that changed how the world creates images and video. We're creating the generative models that power how people make images and video—tools used by millions of creators, developers, and businesses worldwide. Our FLUX models are among the most advanced in the world, and we're just getting started.

Headquartered in Freiburg, Germany with a growing presence in San Francisco, we're scaling fast while staying true to what makes us different: research excellence, open science, and building technology that expands human creativity.

Why this role

FLUX models ship as open weights, which gives anyone full access to the model. Our safety efforts focus on suppressing harmful behaviors and mitigating the risk of misuse, so safety has to be built into the models themselves, not bolted on afterwards.

As a Member of Technical Staff on our safety research team, you'll research and ship methods that make FLUX models safe by design: from what goes into the training data to how the models are mid- and post-trained, across images, video and the text that conditions them. This is a role with real ownership: you won't just do research on model safety, you'll shape it. The methods you build ship in FLUX models with over 75 million downloads on Hugging Face and in production at some of the largest platforms in the world.

What you'll work on

- Develop mid- and post-training safety methods for FLUX models, such as safety SFT, preference optimization and RL with safety rewards, and concept erasure.

- Build safety data filtering that runs at pretraining scale: classifiers and pipelines that screen billions of images, video clips and captions, with measured Pareto frontiers and precision/recall trade-offs.

- Make safety hold up for open-weight releases, including robustness to adversarial prompts and to downstream fine-tuning.

- Extend safety to the text side of the stack: prompts, captions and the text encoders that condition our models.

- Design evaluations and red-teaming that measure harmful generations alongside image quality and prompt following, so safety gains don't come at the cost of performance.

- Work directly with pretraining and post-training teams so your methods land in the release model, and publish where it makes sense.

What we're looking for

- Hands-on research experience in visual safety: safety of text-to-image, text-to-video or vision-language models, such as harm classifiers, safe generation methods or safety benchmarks.

- Proven experience in at least one of:

- Large-scale safety data filtering: building and running classifiers or filtering pipelines over hundreds of millions of samples or more.

- Safety mid- or post-training: safety SFT, DPO or RL with safety objectives, or unlearning applied to large generative models.

- Deep familiarity with concept erasure methods (e.g. ESD, UCE, adversarial unlearning) and their failure modes, such as concept recovery and collateral damage to unrelated concepts.

- Track record of shipping: top-venue publications (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV) paired with production impact, or unambiguous production wins at a frontier lab.

- Experience with distributed training at multi-node scale.

- Strong PyTorch fluency; you write research code that others can build on. You work fluently with coding agents to move faster, and have the depth to verify their output and own the result.

- Experience running multi-agent workflows: you know which tasks to hand off and which to keep yourself, and you use the speed-up to raise the quality bar, not lower it.

We'd be especially excited if you:

- Know how to keep safety intact after release, when others fine-tune open weights.

- Have tackled safety for video generation, where harm can emerge across frames rather than in any single frame.

- Bring experience with audio safety, especially for jointly generated audio and video, where each modality can amplify harm in the other.

- Have unlearned concepts from text encoders or built safety-tuned encoders (e.g. Safe-CLIP-style approaches).

- Have worked on text safety: LLM safety tuning, prompt and jailbreak defenses, or text safety classifiers, ideally across languages.

- Have applied latent-space safety methods, such as activation steering or safe guidance.

- Have built VLM-based safety judges or guard models for filtering or evaluation.

How we work together

We're a distributed team with real offices that people actually use. You'll join us in Freiburg at least 2 days a week (or one full week every other week). We'll cover reasonable travel costs to make this possible. We think in-person time matters, and we've structured things to make it accessible to all. We'll discuss what this will look like for the role during our interview process.

Everything we do is grounded in four values:

- Obsessed. We are a frontier research lab. The science has to be right, the understanding deep, the product beautiful.

- Low Ego. The work speaks. The best idea wins, no matter who said it. Credit is shared. Nobody is above any task.

- Bold. We take the ambitious bet. We ship, we do not wait for conditions to be perfect.

- Kind. People over politics. We treat each other with genuine warmth. Agency without empathy creates chaos.

If this sounds like work you'd enjoy, we'd love to hear from you.

Compensation 

EUR 160K-220K + equity, depending on profile

title: Senior Software Engineer, Verticals (AI Native)
description:
Headquarters: Canada

URL: http://www.life360.com 

About Life360

Life360’s mission is to keep people close to the ones they love. Our category-leading mobile app, Tile tracking devices, and Pet GPS tracker empower members to protect the people, pets, and things they care about most with a range of services, including location sharing, safe driver reports, and crash detection with emergency dispatch. Life360 serves approximately 107.7 million monthly active users (MAU), as of September 30, 2026, across more than 180 countries. 

Life360 delivers peace of mind and enhances everyday family life with seamless coordination for all the moments that matter, big and small. By continuing to innovate and deliver for our customers, we have become a household name and the must-have mobile-based membership for families (and those friends who are basically family).

Life360 has more than 500 (and growing!) remote-first employees. For more information, please visit life360.com .

Life360 is a Remote First company, which means a remote work environment will be the primary experience for all employees. All positions, unless otherwise specified, can be performed remotely (within the US and Canada) regardless of any specified location above. 

We are AI Native

We are building an AI native company where AI is an integral part of how we build and operate. AI tool usage during interviews varies by role. You may be asked to demonstrate proficiency with AI tools, discuss how you leverage AI, or complete interview exercises without AI assistance. Your Recruiter will provide clear guidance as you move through the interview process.

Undisclosed use of AI not previously discussed with or approved by your Recruiter may impact your candidacy.

About The Team

This role sits on the Verticals team within Life360 — the group building the next frontier of meaningful connection beyond the core family circle. This role's initial focus is Aging in Place: helping aging parents stay safely independent while giving the families around them real peace of mind. Over time, this role may flex to support other emerging verticals — Things (Tile, connected trackers) or Pets — as priorities shift, so we're looking for someone who wants to help define the pattern for new member segments, not just ship one feature set.

We are a product-minded, AI-Native engineering team. That means AI isn't just a tool we use — it's how we work. We've redesigned our team workflows around AI, treating it as a first-class collaborator at every stage: ideation, coding, testing, review, and iteration. We ship faster and go deeper because of it, and we're looking for someone who wants to help define what that looks like at scale.

About the Job

Life360 is hiring an AI Native Senior Software Engineer — a senior engineer who doesn't just use AI tools, but thinks natively in them. You'll be central to how the Verticals team builds products.

You'll design and build features that serve one of our most important and fastest-growing member segments: aging parents who want to stay safely connected with, and independent from, the families who care about them. As priorities change, you may also apply these same patterns to Things (connected trackers) or Pets.

You will take full ownership of what you build from the first line of code through production, on-call, and the member impact it has. You obsess over the humans on the other end of the product, not just the ticket.

Full-stack experience is required for this role — you should be comfortable moving between backend services and the mobile surfaces that expose them. Our stack spans Spring Boot microservices, Java, Kafka, and Kafka Streams on the backend, a modern cloud-native platform on AWS, and native iOS (Swift) and Android (Kotlin) apps on the client side.

In your first year, success looks like having shipped end-to-end features serving the Aging in Place member segment and establishing at least one AI-native workflow the broader team adopts.

For candidates based in the US, the salary range for this position is $103,500 to $192,000 USD. For candidates based out of Canada, the salary range for this position is 149,500 to 177,500 CAD. Note: Please be aware that the job title for positions in Canada will be "Developer" in lieu of "Engineer." We take into consideration an individual's background, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience in determining final salary. Base pay may also vary based on geographic location, with US work locations falling into one of three geographic tiers. 

Total compensation is inclusive of equity compensation in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) , as well as a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, financial, and other benefits. 

What You’ll Do

- Ship end-to-end across the stack — from backend services and APIs through to the iOS and Android surfaces members use, serving tens of millions of users — moving between layers as the feature demands.

- Work with AI (Claude Code) as a first-class collaborator — orchestrate agents to create specs, generate code, and perform reviews, moving faster without sacrificing quality.

- Define and codify AI-Native engineering practices for the Verticals team, establishing playbooks the broader org can adopt.

- Collaborate closely with product managers and designers to turn complex user problems into scalable engineering solutions.

- Contribute to architectural decisions, code reviews, and a culture of craft and continuous improvement.

- Participate in on-call rotation and incident response.

- Mentor team members and contribute to team processes and technical standards.

- Support performance, reliability, and accessibility across the features you own.

- Adapt patterns and services built for Aging in Place to future verticals (Things, Pets) as team scope expands.

What We’re Looking For

- 4+ years of experience building and operating high-quality, consumer-scale services.

- 1+ years of hands-on experience prompting, evaluating, and building with LLMs.

- Full-stack proficiency spanning backend services (Java, Spring Boot, Kafka) and mobile client development (Swift for iOS and/or Kotlin for Android), with the versatility to work across the whole stack as needed.

- Hands-on experience with agentic workflows, prompt engineering, context window management, and MCP/function calling.

- A track record of using AI tooling to multiply your own output — not just as autocomplete, but as a development partner.

- A strong sense of ownership — you don't wait to be told what to fix, and you follow through past "it works on my machine" to "it works for the member, in production, at scale."

- Strong communication and collaboration skills — you work well with product, design, and platform engineers.

- Excitement for defining what it means to be AI-Native — you're not waiting for the playbook, you want to write it.

- Empathy for the humans behind the product — an aging parent trying to stay independent, or a family member trying to help from afar.

- Bachelor's Degree in a Technical field, or equivalent experience.

Nice-to-Have 

- Experience with IoT, telematics, or embedded/hardware-adjacent systems.

- Familiarity with Kafka, Kinesis, or other high-throughput streaming platforms.

- Background with observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, DataDog).

AI-Native Expectations

We use AI coding tools as a professional standard on this team. Here's what that means in practice:

- Daily use: You use AI coding assistants (we support Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot) for real, substantive tasks: analysis, coding, refactoring, testing, navigating codebases, and documentation. Not just research or autocomplete but as a development partner.

- Judgment and ownership: AI-generated code gets the same review you'd give any PR. You are accountable for everything you ship.

- Velocity: We expect senior engineers who use AI well to operate with meaningful leverage — doing more with the same time, taking on problems that would otherwise require a larger team.

- Team leadership: You share what works. You automate prompting strategies that others can build on and help teammates earlier in their AI workflow adoption get up to speed.

- Continuous learning: The tooling is changing fast. You stay current and bring recommendations to the team when something would meaningfully improve how we work.

Our Benefits

- Medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance plans (100% paid for US employees). We offer life and disability as well as supplemental plans for medical and dental for Canadian employees.

- 401(k) plan with company matching program in the US and RRSP with DPSP plan for Canadian employees.

- Paid parental leave.

- Mental Wellness Program & Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for mental well-being.

- Generous time off: flexible PTO, companywide holidays throughout the year plus summer and winter shutdowns.

- Learning & Development programs.

- Equipment, tools, and reimbursement support for a productive remote environment.

- Free Life360 Platinum Membership and Tile trackers.

AI Usage: We use AI to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Life360 hiring teams

Life360 Values

Our company’s mission-driven culture is guided by our shared values to create a trusted work environment where you can bring your authentic self to work and make a positive difference 

- Be a Good Person - We have a team of high integrity people you can trust. 

- Be Direct With Respect - We communicate directly, even when it’s hard.

Our Commitment to Belonging

We don’t discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, or any other legally protected status. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms. 

About the OS Integration team: 

The OS Integration team ensures Firefox works well with the host operating system and environment. We’re a distributed team with expertise in Windows, macOS, and Linux-based operating systems. Our responsibilities include developing fixes and improvements for Firefox related to Windows, macOS, and Linux environments. This might include integration with a new OS feature or fixing an OS-specific user interface bug. Other responsibilities include native crash reporting, OS abstraction layers, sandboxing, hardening, installer, updater, device APIs, and enterprise DLP support.

The role will lean on your Windows expertise, but projects may have a cross-platform component. This role will include development of features for Firefox in enterprise environments especially implementation of Data Loss Prevention (DLP) features. As a Staff Software Engineer, you’re a clear communicator and expert in your domain, ready to work on multi-month projects. You’ll contribute to the team through code review, mentoring, and discussion. 

What you’ll do: 

- Improve the quality of Firefox and other Mozilla products by debugging and fixing software defects, improving the browsing experience for hundreds of millions of users. 

- Lead projects that improve the stability, security, and performance of Firefox. 

- Collaborate with experienced software engineers. 

- Perform code reviews and provide technical direction. 

- Work with a geographically-distributed development team. 

- Interact with teams throughout the organization. 

What you’ll bring:

- Knowledge of web technologies such as Javascript, HTML, and CSS.

title: Spacecraft Thermal Engineer
description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecraft for humanity.

We are seeking a Spacecraft Thermal Engineer to join our Thermal Control System team. You will contribute to the preparation, execution and analysis of thermal verification activities, including Thermal Vacuum (TVAC) and Thermal Balance testing, and support spacecraft assembly, integration and test. Alongside these activities, you will take technical ownership of assigned thermal control products, following their development, supplier activities, qualification and delivery for integration.

You will work closely with AIT, suppliers, external test facilities and other subsystem teams. You will be part of the TCS & ECLSS Team and report to the Principal Thermal Control System Engineer.

Key Responsibilities:

Product Ownership and Supplier Follow-up

- Take technical ownership of assigned thermal control products, from requirements and interface definition through qualification and delivery for integration, with guidance from senior engineers.

- Act as the day-to-day technical interface with suppliers, following design, manufacturing, testing and delivery activities.

- Review supplier deliverables, including design justifications, test procedures and reports, against agreed requirements.

- Maintain product requirements, interfaces, configuration information and technical documentation.

- Prepare product review documentation and coordinate the closure of review actions.

- Track product maturity, technical risks and delivery milestones, escalating issues affecting performance, cost or schedule.

- Coordinate with AIT to ensure hardware is delivered with the appropriate configuration, documentation and verification status.

Thermal Testing and Verification

- Contribute to the definition of thermal test objectives, configurations and success criteria.

- Prepare test plans, procedures and instrumentation requirements in coordination with AIT and test facilities.

- Support spacecraft-level TVAC and Thermal Balance campaigns, and coordinate testing activities for assigned thermal control products.

- Contribute to test readiness reviews, test execution and anomaly investigations.

- Prepare test reports and verification evidence, maintaining traceability to applicable requirements.

- Track verification activities and follow technical actions through to closure within your assigned scope.

Flight Model Integration and AIT Support

- Work alongside AIT teams during the installation, integration and verification of thermal control hardware.

- Contribute to integration procedures, thermal instrumentation layouts and test configurations.

- Support functional testing, troubleshooting and spacecraft system check-outs.

- Support leak testing and fluid loop commissioning, as applicable to assigned activities.

- Investigate integration issues with the relevant engineering, supplier and quality teams.

Thermal Test Data Analysis

- Support pre-test thermal predictions in collaboration with thermal analysts.

- Process and analyse test data to assess hardware and system performance against requirements.

- Contribute to thermal model correlation and the investigation of discrepancies between predictions and test results.

- Recommend design or test improvements and capture lessons learned.

What We Would Love to See from You

Qualifications:

- Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Thermodynamics or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

- 3+ years of relevant experience in spacecraft thermal engineering, including thermal hardware development, integration or testing.

- Hands-on experience contributing to thermal test campaigns, such as TVAC or Thermal Balance testing.

- Good understanding of spacecraft thermal control hardware, such as MLI, temperature sensors, heaters and fluid loop components.

- Familiarity with spacecraft qualification and acceptance processes, requirements traceability and verification documentation.

- Experience contributing to hardware development or supplier follow-up, including reviewing technical documentation and tracking actions.

- Familiarity with thermal instrumentation, data acquisition systems and test facility interfaces.

- Experience processing and analysing engineering data using Python, MATLAB or equivalent tools.

- Familiarity with applicable space engineering standards, including ECSS and NASA ones.

- Fluent in English. German, French and Italian are an asset.

Skills and Behaviors:

- Ownership mindset, with the ability to drive assigned activities to completion and seek support when needed.

- Strong analytical and practical problem-solving skills.

title: DFT Engineer
description:
Meet Arago and the Aragonians 

Arago’s mission is to re-engineer the foundations of computing from first principles.

The explosive growth of AI is pushing the industry to rethink how processors are built. Arago is meeting that challenge with a proprietary technology that fuses optical and CMOS technologies to deliver an order-of-magnitude increase in performance.

Arago is the fastest, and currently the only, company to have built such a processor. What you’ll do 

As DFT Engineer, you will define and own the Design-for-Test strategy of our next-generation SoC from the ground up. This is not a role where you inherit an existing flow, scripts, or team — you build it. You will work closely with RTL design, physical implementation, and our test partners to make our chips manufacturable, testable, and ready for volume production.

Required Skills and Experience 

- 10+ years in DFT, with at least one full SoC tape-out owned end-to-end — not just one slice of a large team effort.

- Strong hands-on experience with one major DFT suite: Siemens Tessent, Synopsys TestMAX / DFTMAX / TetraMAX, or Cadence Modus.

- Scan insertion and test compression (EDT / DFTMAX / Modus-type).

- MBIST and memory repair integration.

- JTAG / IEEE 1149.1, IEEE 1687 (IJTAG), IEEE 1500 wrappers.

- ATPG pattern generation (stuck-at, transition, path delay), coverage analysis and improvement.

- DFT verification: gate-level simulation of patterns, timing-aware checks.

- Test-mode SDC / STA understanding.

- Scripting: Tcl, Python.

- Experience in silicon bring-up and ATE debug.

- Language: English at a proficient level.

Responsibilities 

- Define DFT architecture and test strategy — coverage targets, test time, pin budget — in collaboration with Siemens experts and our design team.

- Implement hands-on: scan insertion, compression, MBIST, JTAG/IJTAG/IEEE 1500 wrappers, ATPG, sign-off.

- Drive DFT verification: gate-level simulation of test patterns and timing-aware checks.

- Support physical design and STA for test modes — constraints, scan timing closure.

- Be the bridge between RTL design, physical implementation, and the ATE / test house for silicon bring-up.

- Deliver patterns to ATE and debug failing patterns with the test house.

- Contribute to DFT tool evaluation and set up a reusable, scalable flow.

Preferred Qualification 

- Experience at advanced nodes (7nm and below).

- Experience with large AI/HPC or multi-core SoCs, NoC-based designs.

- Hierarchical DFT on large designs.

- Has participated in a DFT tool selection or flow setup from scratch.

- Logic BIST, in-system test, or functional safety (ISO 26262) exposure.

- Yield analysis and diagnosis (e.g. Tessent Diagnosis, YieldInsight).

Pay and benefits

- Meaningful stock option plan offered (included in the majority of full time offers).

- Healthcare coverage (including family-friendly options), pension contributions, professional development support, and 25 days of PTO, in addition to public holidays.

- Ownership of a key technical domain, with significant vertical and/or horizontal growth opportunities, based on performance and individual drive.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of AI at Arago.

title: Engineering Intern
description:
About Atira

Atira builds the commercial brain for industrials. Our agents 10x the sales engineers of today by offering the complete toolbox of tasks needed in complex environments. They handle everything from extracting and classifying requirements from incoming RFQs, orchestrating communication and information retrieval across multiple stakeholders and systems, while generating outcomes like documentation, production system inputs, or configuration recommendations. CRM. Atira. ERP. 

We are one of the fastest growing teams in Munich and are looking for you to join us!

Why engineers are the foundation of everything Atira ships

As an Engineering Intern at Atira, you will work on frontier AI technology, such as (recursive) agent harnesses, runtimes, evals, inference and self-verification in complex engineering domains. You build the frameworks, primitives and scaffolding that let agents reliably handle complex industrial processes end to end, from the first inbound RFQ to the write-back into ERP.

Misreading or wrongly interpreting a spec can cost a manufacturer six figures, so the challenges are real and the margin for error is thin.

Where you trained matters less than what you've built and how clearly you can describe what broke. Atira is at a stage where you must own problems end to end, because what you ship today is what our customers use tomorrow.

What you will do

- Work on the agent runtime and harnesses. You improve the core components that let Atira's agents reason in complex engineering environments across the entire sales-engineering lifecycle, orchestrate themselves recursively at scale through dynamic programs, and handle arbitrarily large amounts of data. This includes the runtime/sandboxing, the harness, and the outer orchestration layer that ties it together

- Build out our AI moat. You are in charge of improving quality & evals, improving the ontology layer that unlocks compounding process knowledge and fusing deterministic guardrails with agentic agency to make our agents actionable at enterprise level complexity

- Unlock industrial scale. Industrials live in multi-modal, data-heavy environments: 1000-page inbounds, pricing lists, CAD files, ERP tables, legacy applications. You scale the AI systems behind them to millions of concurrent LLM requests in isolated sandboxes, with no silent failures, cost blowouts or latency explosions.

- Advance our internal tooling. FDEs, platform engineers and the GTM team depend on tooling you build to improve Atira's internal context layer, ambient agents, insight and observability engines

- Work with FDEs when customer problems hit the platform. When an FDE hits a problem they should be able to pull you in. At a team of 20, the boundary between AI, platform and customer is thin, and you'll cross it regularly

What we are looking for

Ownership, depth, and the instinct to take problems personally, go deep until you understand the system, and own the outcome including the parts that broke.

Your profile

- Agent fluency sits on top of real engineering fundamentals. Solid skills in Python, TypeScript, or a comparable language. We value someone that can still code without AI. Ideally paired with hands-on experience with agents, evals, harnesses, runtimes, sandboxing and tools

- You've gone further than most with AI-assisted development. Whether it's Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or your own setup, you've invested seriously in building the skills, context, and workflows to get maximum leverage from coding agents. This isn't a nice-to-have. We think engineers who have mastered this are fundamentally more productive, and we hire accordingly

- You reason clearly about technical tradeoffs. You don’t need to have run systems at scale yet, but you can think through how a design would hold up at thousands of requests per second and explain the pros and cons of different approaches. Every design has tradeoffs: no free lunch

- You’ve demonstrated ownership and initiative. A side project you took further than anyone asked, a serious open-source contribution, a research project or a startup. We want evidence that you build without being told to and can explain what broke and why

- You have a strong technical foundation. Enrolled or recently graduated in Computer Science, Information Systems, AI, or a related technical field from a strong technical university (cracked dropouts can qualify too though)

- Full working proficiency in English. German is not required

- You're ready for a real internship, not a side gig. You can commit to at least three months full-time, on-site in Munich

What you'll get

- Real ownership: you'll be one of the early team members and shape both product and architecture as well as work closely with customers

- Strong peers and mentorship: work with and learn from engineers who have shipped AI systems in industrial environments at scale, with the opportunity for mentorship along the way

- Impactful work: your code is deployed all across Europe’s and US industrial backbone, affecting how complex products and services are sold and configured worldwide

- Competitive salary and additional benefits

- Most importantly: Collaborate & thrive in a high-performing but caring culture. We will own the industrial sales function but will do so with modesty and integrity

What success looks like at the end of the internship

- You've shipped meaningful improvements to the agent runtime, our AI pipelines and related systems that are running in production across multiple customer deployments

- You own one well-defined piece of our AI stack end to end (an eval suite, an internal tool, part of the context layer or the SDK), and the team trusts your judgment on how it should evolve

- When something breaks in the part you own, you can trace it end to end, from agent behaviour back to the agent infrastructure layer, and fix it

- You’ve made an improvement to our internal AI tooling that the team now uses day to day

- The design decisions in your piece have held up under real load, and you can explain the tradeoffs you made and what you’d do differently

- If these metrics are met, we'd take you full-time without thinking twice

title: General Capabilities - Member of Technical Staff
description:
About Us 

We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity.

Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next.

The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve.

Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost.

Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor.

In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence.

We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role 

Callosum believes that orders of magnitude improvements in AI systems will come through application-aware orchestration across heterogeneous models and hardware. The General Capabilities team is developing the science that makes that possible: a principled, evidence-based method for building agentic systems automatically.

We are hiring for several positions on this team through one application. Depending on your background, you will work on our agent runtime, on evaluation, or on automated agentic system optimisation. We are looking for experienced systems engineers and researchers. Since we are an interdisciplinary team, we expect depth in one area and a willingness to work across the others.

What You'll Build 

Depending on the position, you will work on some of the following:

- Design and build stateful, asynchronous agent runtimes across distributed environments

- Develop clear Python APIs, libraries, and DSLs with stable extension points for tools, backends, and new execution models.

- Develop evaluation and observability tooling for long-horizon, tool-using agents.

- Research methods that improve agents automatically, such as program search, routing, context management, multi-agent collaboration and post-training.

- Work with our infrastructure teams to optimise agents for cost and latency on heterogeneous hardware.

What Sets You Apart 

We are seeking candidates with demonstrable experience in one or more of these areas:

- Experience building runtimes, workflow engines, distributed systems or developer frameworks that other engineers adopted.

- Deep familiarity with the internals of SGLang, vLLM or comparable inference serving frameworks: scheduler design, memory management and execution pipelines.

- Depth in multi-agent systems, program synthesis, or evolutionary and LLM-driven search over programs and agents, including systems that run the research loop themselves.

- Experience with RL or post-training for long-horizon, multi-step or tool-use tasks.

- Evaluations, benchmarks or agent harnesses you built that other people went on to use.

What We Offer 

- Competitive Salary, determined by skills and experience

- Equity & Ownership

- Private healthcare

- We offer Visa sponsorship and relocation benefits to hire the best in the world

- We work in person at our London office. You'll have the tools, space and setup to do your best work, and if you have specific needs, just tell us

We're committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome, and believe in equal opportunities for all.

title: Platform Engineer - Data Resilience and Recovery platform
description:
Build and own a self-service, multi-tenant platform that keeps the critical data of 20+ customers recoverable

Do you like building platforms that other teams consume, at scale, across private and public clouds, with security and tenant isolation as non-negotiables? At Schuberg Philis, the world is shifting from traditional backup to data security and resilience. We’re looking for a Platform Engineer to strengthen our Data Management-as-a-Service (DMS) team and help us build the next generation of our platform.

About the Team

The DMS team builds and runs a shared, fully segregated data resilience platform that serves more than 20 of our customers. Customer teams consume it through self-service, and they handle their own day-to-day backup and restore operations. That means you won’t spend your days on job monitoring, restore tickets or backup schedules. Your customers are internal and external engineering teams, and your product is the platform they build on.

You’ll join a dedicated group of data security experts within our larger Services Team and work closely with our sbp.cloud team, who operate our self-built sovereign cloud solutions. With our plan-build-run approach, you take end-to-end ownership: you design it, you build it, you run it.

The Challenge

Running one platform for 20+ customers means solving the hard problems of platform engineering:

- Multi-tenancy by design: strict isolation of data, access, and performance between customers, on shared infrastructure.

- Self-service at scale: APIs, guardrails and automation that let customer teams onboard and operate independently, without tickets.

- Scale and resilience: 4,000+ protected endpoints and more than 25,000 recovery points generated daily, on a dedicated private cloud spanning multiple availability zones.

- Heterogeneous workloads: Oracle, MS-SQL, SAP, Sybase, PaaS, container platforms and VMs across VMware VCF, OpenStack, AWS, Azure and Kubernetes.

- Modern storage back-ends: public cloud services and S3-compatible object storage built on Pure FlashBlade//S and NetApp StorageGRID in our own datacenters, plus a long-term archiving tier.

- Security first: immutability, segregation and hardening in a highly secure environment where recoverability is the ultimate guarantee.

Your Role

As a Platform Engineer, you take full responsibility for the lifecycle of the platform: architecture, deployment, evolution and reliability. You treat the platform as a product: you improve features, drive innovation and keep the user experience of customer teams in mind. You work closely with technology vendors (primarily Commvault) and push their product teams to improve, while applying standardized guardrails, driving automation and following best-in-class practices.

Your focus is on making day-2 operations simple and cost-effective, so there is room to implement new security features, streamline customer onboarding and enable new projects. You also guide customers in their data protection needs, contribute to RFIs/RFPs, and help scope and design new solutions.

What You’ll Do

- Own the architecture and lifecycle of a multi-tenant data resilience platform, in line with our plan-build-run methodology.

- Design and ship self-service capabilities that customer teams use independently, end to end.

- Automate everything repeatable: deployments, tenant onboarding, configuration and platform operations, using Infrastructure as Code.

- Ensure platform availability, aiming for 100% uptime and maximum customer satisfaction.

- Evolve a diverse storage back-end across public cloud and on-prem S3-compatible solutions.

- Enable customers to protect workloads on VMware VCF, OpenStack, AWS, Azure, Kubernetes and more.

- Work with vendor product teams and drive their roadmaps.

- Provide hands-on advisory and technical support, contribute to RFI/RFP processes, and help design new solutions.

Who Are You?

- First and foremost, you are a platform engineer at heart, and you like building things other engineers rely on. A passion for data protection, security and resilience is a plus, and you’ll grow it here.

- You enjoy teamwork, thrive on challenges and like collaborating with both peers and customers.

- You’re comfortable in highly secure, complex environments.

- You have a solid understanding of multi-tenant architectures and security concepts.

- You are proficient in Linux and/or Windows ecosystems.

- You have experience across private (VMware/OpenStack) and public cloud platforms (Azure, AWS).

- You’re skilled in Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Ansible and/or Chef) and in scripting and automation (Python, Bash, PowerShell, etc.).

- Experience with data management/protection tools is valuable, whether Commvault, Rubrik or similar, but not a must. We’ll teach you the domain; you bring the engineering craft.

More information?

As a Senior AI R&D Engineer in Model Training (f/m/d), you will join our model training team in Heidelberg or Berlin. Most of the team is based in Heidelberg. The model training team is building and improving our model training pipeline, which has been used to train Kolibri. 

- You will work across our full stack. Some weeks you might be optimizing how training loads are scheduled on our cluster and making the pipeline more robust and performant so we can iterate faster. Other weeks, you will be enabling large-scale code execution for reinforcement learning. And at other times, you might dig deep into our evaluation codebase to lift inference throughput on evals.

- No two days are the same. Things move fast, and your ability to focus and prioritize is what lets you unblock the team day-to-day while designing the high-quality tooling and infrastructure that speeds us up long-term.

- Identifying issues and taking initiative is what drives our day-to-day work.

- Working mode, design decisions, priorities are all done in your team together with your team mates. 
The strongest teams often use highly collaborative techniques, like mob or pair programming.

- Due to the highly collaborative nature of our work you are expected to be on-site at least two days a week. If you are in Berlin, you should expect to travel around every second month for a few days to Heidelberg.

- We are specifically looking to strengthen the Software Engineering in the teams which are research heavy. Major points include improving the maintainability of our code through tests and design & architecture changes.

Requirements 

- At its core, you need to be able to dive into a codebase, change the behavior as necessary, and after the change the code should be better tested and easier to understand than before.

- As such we look for candidates for an understanding of how to design for low coupling and high cohesion paired with the ability to incrementally refactor.

- Experience with the following technologies is likely to be helpful:

- Test Driven Development (TDD)

- Trunk based development

- Continuous integration

- Domain Driven Design

Nice-to-haves

- Masters degree in engineering, robotics, computer science, or a related technical or management field.

title: CDI - Senior Context & Analytics Engineer - Paris
description:
Mission 

Un agent ne vaut que ce que valent les données et les connaissances sur lesquelles il répond. Pipelines, modèles de données, définitions de métriques, droits d’accès : vous créez et gouvernez ce socle, et les applications et les agents de nos clients s’appuient dessus. Quand un analyste ou un agent demande un chiffre, la réponse est celle de l’équipe finance, accompagnée de sa définition et de sa source.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez que les métiers et les agents puissent se fier aux données, et les utilisent. 

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype Context & Analytics Engineer.

Activités et responsabilités 

Avec les équipes métier et les analystes, il s’agit de définir ce que signifie chaque métrique et de vérifier que les données y correspondent. Sur ce socle, les Product Engineers et les AI Engineers construisent applications et agents.

Les Platform Engineers exploitent l’infrastructure sur laquelle tournent vos pipelines. Les échanges avec les data owners et les équipes de gouvernance du client, la relecture de code entre pairs et l’accompagnement des nouvelles recrues complètent le quotidien.

Vos responsabilités : 

- Construire des pipelines d’ingestion et des modèles de données, avec dbt par exemple.

- Mettre en place des contrôles de qualité des données et maintenir le lineage.

- Construire la couche sémantique et les définitions de métriques, pour que les personnes et les agents utilisent les mêmes chiffres, y compris en text-to-SQL.

- Définir les règles de gouvernance et les droits d’accès.

- Construire des pipelines de connaissances pour le RAG : indexation, chunking, métadonnées, permissions.

- Préparer le contexte exploitable par les agents : métadonnées, définitions, lineage et permissions.

Profil recherché 

Les indispensables : 

- Vous écrivez du SQL avec aisance et modélisez les données pour l’analyse.

- Des pipelines de données planifiés, testés et surveillés figurent à votre actif.

- Aux côtés des équipes métier, vous définissez les métriques et vérifiez que les données veulent bien dire ce que tout le monde croit y lire.

- La qualité des données, la documentation et les droits d’accès comptent pour vous.

- Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.

Un plus, pas un prérequis : 

- Python pour le traitement de données.

- Une plateforme de données cloud, comme BigQuery, Snowflake ou Databricks.

- Une couche sémantique ou un metrics store.

- La préparation de documents pour le RAG : chunking, indexation, métadonnées.

- Des outils de data catalogue ou de lineage.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? 

Dans un métier où deux tableaux de bord affichent parfois deux chiffres différents, ce poste consiste à rétablir la confiance : un chiffre juste, une définition partagée, une source identifiable. Ce travail, discret quand il réussit, conditionne tout ce que les autres archétypes construisent au-dessus.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’apprend sur les projets, avec les AI Engineers et l’appui de la communauté Context & Analytics Engineer, notamment le context engineering, c’est-à-dire le travail qui rend les données exploitables par les agents d’IA. À partir de 2027, l’archétype Context & Analytics Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (évaluation de l’IA, responsabilité en production).

Plus tard, un rôle transverse devient possible (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), tout comme les chapters AI Architect et AI Product Manager.

Processus de recrutement 

Le processus demande environ quatre heures, réparties en six étapes dont une seule sur site.

- Entretien RH (45 min, à distance) : parcours, motivations et points pratiques, comme le calendrier et les prétentions salariales.

- Appel avec le CTO (15 à 30 min, à distance).

- Screening technique (30 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter AI Applied Engineer) : retour détaillé sur vos projets passés, puis questions techniques et de design de solution.

- Code review et live coding (60 min, sur site, avec un membre du chapter) : relecture d’un dépôt de code existant et correction de ses défauts, puis construction d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité avec un coding agent et présentation du résultat.

- Cas technique (45 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter) : cadrage d’un problème métier, proposition d’une solution technique, description de la méthode d’évaluation, puis discussion de vos choix.

- Entretien final (30 min, à distance, avec une personne de l’encadrement du département, Engineering Manager ou Director) : reprise des points restés ouverts, choix de l’archétype et du niveau les mieux adaptés à votre profil, et réponses à toutes vos questions.

Selon les étapes, tous les outils d’IA sont autorisés, ou aucun. Lors du live coding, c’est la manière de travailler avec l’assistance de l’IA qui est observée.

Rémunération : 53 000€ à 70 000€ brut annuel (fixe) + variable selon expérience et séniorité

Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel. Nos recrutements reposent sur les compétences, le potentiel et l’adéquation avec le rôle.

title: Software Engineer - Delta Platform
description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous! 

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. 

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. 

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. 

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. 

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. 

About the role

Delta builds BLP’s core software: the technical foundation that everything else at the company runs on.

Who we're looking for

Modelling logic and correctness by construction is paramount to us. We aim to express what must be true, prevent invalid states, and keep systems pristine even as they grow.

Thus, we’re looking for highly ambitious engineers who can tackle difficult problems and think precisely. You must be able to make assumptions explicit and use formal, structured reasoning to reach a solution, and explain why it is correct. Typically, strong background in mathematics is a key foundation for this kind of work. We also place a high value on thoroughness and perfectionism.

Tooling wise, we rely heavily on type systems & functional programming.

What you'll do

Our work spans four areas, you will usually work on a given project within one of:

- Infrastructure: Build and operate the cloud infrastructure BLP depends on, covering security, observability and CI/CD.

- Backend: Develop a large codebase, tackling performance, concurrency and the challenges of distributed systems.

- ML: Apply the latest AI technology to complex, real-world business problems and turn it into reliable production software.

- Unbound: Build our product extension platform, enabling BLP to automate arbitrary customer business processes as we scale.

What you'll bring

We do not require experience with any particular technology or even industry software development experience.

You should, however, provide clear evidence of the abilities we’re looking for. That evidence could include:

- strong academic backgrounds (math PhD/MSc or significant olympiad achievements)

- startup experience (early employee, built productive systems yourself & know what it takes to maintain them)

- FP experience (have deep understanding of programming languages and are able to discern the various tradeoffs of different paradigms)

Flexibility. Work on-site in Zurich or remotely within Europe.

Learn more about blp and our values at blp.digital/company/careers .

We deliver health, performance, video, and AI insights from the locker room to competitive environments, ensuring every decision is an opportunity to gain an advantage, sharpen performance, and build lasting success. 

WE WANT PEOPLE WHO ARE PASSIONATE ABOUT SOLVING HARD PROBLEMS 

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help build the Perch camera system,

title: Senior Power Electronics Engineer
description:
About Us 

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the Role 

Power electronics are the bottleneck on every next-generation UAS airframe we build: motor controllers, gate drivers, and DC-DC stages are what define flight time, payload, thermal envelope, and field reliability. We're looking for a senior IC to own the analog power chain end-to-end across our UXV platforms: from MOSFET commutation simulation through PCB layout to lab validation. You will be the technical reference on power electronics inside our Lausanne engineering hub, unblocking propulsion, airframe, and embedded teams in parallel as we scale from prototype cadence to multi-platform deployment.

This is a builder role, not a research seat. You ship hardware.

Responsibilities 

- Power Stage Architecture: Lead motor-controller and DC-DC topology across fixed-wing, multicopter, and hybrid UXV platforms. Translate mission constraints into power-chain specification.

- MOSFET Commutation & Gate-Drive Design: Own the analog switching design: dead-time tuning, gate shaping, switching-loss vs EMI vs thermal trade-offs.

- Multi-fidelity Simulation: Deploy the full stack: analytical loss budgeting, transient SPICE (LTspice), system-level modelling in PLECS or Simulink.

- BLDC Drive Stages: Design three-phase inverters with integrated current sensing, protection, Trapezoidal and FOC-aware hardware interfaces.

- High-Power-Density PCBA: Lead schematic and layout in Altium or KiCad with thermal, parasitics, and EMC engineered in from the first revision.

- EMI / EMC Engineering: Drive pre-compliance, filter design, and root-cause debug under flight-representative loads.

- Prototype-to-Production: Take motor-controller PCBAs through revision discipline, DFM, and qualification - closing the loop on field returns.

- Lab Validation: Execute bench characterization (power analysers, oscilloscopes, thermal imaging, double-pulse testing) and reconcile against simulation.

- Firmware & Controls Interface: Partner with embedded and propulsion on FOC tuning, current-sense calibration, and the hardware/firmware compensation boundary.

- Design Authority & Mentorship: Set the bar via design-decision records and reference designs. Mentor 1–2 junior engineers.

Candidate Requirements 

- MSc or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, or equivalent.

- 5+ years of hands-on R&D experience on motor drives, BLDC/PMSM controllers, or high-power-density power electronics.

- Deep working mastery of MOSFET commutation design : gate-driver selection, dead-time tuning, switching transitions, loss budgets.

- Proven ownership of at least one motor-controller PCBA shipped from prototype through production (or pre-production qualification) : ideally on drone, robotics, eVTOL, or automotive platforms.

- Fluency in simulation (LTspice, PLECS, or Simulink) and PCB design (Altium).

- Strong, hard-earned intuition for EMI / EMC design and debug.

- Lab-bench discipline: you've personally debugged what simulation missed.

- Comfort with scale-up iteration speed and end-to-end ownership.

- English fluent (working language); French is a nice-to-have, not a requirement.

Bonus points for: GaN / SiC experience, safety-critical design exposure , applied control theory implemented in hardware, exposure to defense, aerospace, or UAS programmes.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.
