title: Cloud Architect
description:
About Vitestro 

Founded in 2017 in Utrecht, Vitestro is pioneering the future of blood collection with the Aletta® Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device™ (ARPD™) . This groundbreaking medical device combines advanced multi-modal imaging (near-infrared, ultrasound, and Doppler ultrasound) with robotics and AI to perform the entire diagnostic blood draw procedure autonomously.

By addressing critical healthcare staffing shortages and improving patient experience, Vitestro is transforming one of the most common and essential medical procedures. With more than 130 team members and growing rapidly, we are scaling our impact. As we placed our first devices with customers, we are now expanding our team to ensure successful implementation and long-term reliability.

At Vitestro, we are committed to continuous innovation and improvement. 

We are looking for a Cloud Architect to shape and implement Vitestro's cloud platform with a clear, pragmatic technical direction. Our infrastructure runs on AWS and supports mission-critical, regulated medical device software. Vitestro is also realizing its first integration with Laboratory Information System (LIS) over the cloud, and delivering that connection is a core part of this role. We need someone who translates real operational and business constraints into working systems — someone whose first instinct is "what does this actually need to do, reliably and affordably," not "what's the most sophisticated way to solve this."

You will join the Platform & Connectivity team and build alongside its cloud, backend, and DevOps engineers. This is an individual-contributor technical leadership role, not a people-management position — you carry the architectural vision and build it hands-on with the team, rather than designing something for others to execute.

If you'd rather ship a solid, working solution than iterate endlessly toward a theoretically ideal one, and you have a track record of keeping cloud costs under control at scale, you'll thrive in this role.

First months at Vitestro 

In your first months, you get to know our cloud platform, the device connectivity and the team. You review the current architecture, its costs and its production-readiness, and identify where the biggest risks and quick wins are. You take ownership of the cloud architecture for our first LIS integration, and you agree with the team on the first architectural standards for observability, logging and infrastructure as code.

This is what success looks like: 

After 12 months, our first LIS integration runs reliably in production, with monitoring, alerting and failure handling in place. Cloud costs are predictable and under control, and key architectural decisions and trade-offs are recorded. The team uses shared patterns instead of reinventing solutions, and is confident running production systems as we move from pre-market to post-market.

Key Responsibilities: 

- Set the technical direction for our AWS-based cloud platform and build it hands-on with the team — weighing cost, operability, and production-readiness as first-class concerns, not afterthoughts

- Own the cloud architecture of Vitestro's first LIS integration over the cloud: secure, reliable, and traceable data exchange between our platform and the hospital laboratory

- Choose solutions on their merits rather than defaulting to the most AWS-native option — including other clouds, self-hosted tooling, or dedicated infrastructure when that's genuinely the better fit

- Take implementations from a working prototype to something that's production-ready — monitoring, alerting, and failure handling included. You bring experience with production systems and advise the team on how to navigate from pre-market to post-market stages.

- Establish architectural standards and patterns so similar problems (e.g. observability, logging, data pipelines) get solved consistently instead of reinvented each time

- Keep cloud costs in check as part of everyday engineering decisions, catching expensive mistakes before they show up on an invoice

- Balance short-term solutions driven by business needs and deadlines against the long-term architecture: make each trade-off explicit, record it, and plan the path from the tactical fix to the durable solution

- Diagnose and resolve production issues across the cloud platform from logs, metrics, and traces

What You’ll Bring: 

- Deep, hands-on production experience with AWS at scale — not certification-level familiarity, but real experience with what breaks and what gets expensive as usage grows

- Proven experience running production systems end to end, from design and release through monitoring and incident response, and the ability to advise a team that is new to production

- Genuine experience building outside an AWS-only mindset — another cloud, self-hosted/open-source alternatives, or dedicated/on-premise infrastructure — enough to make an informed trade-off, not just AWS as the only tool you reach for

- A track record of finishing what others started: turning a partial or unstable implementation into something genuinely reliable in production

- Strong Infrastructure as Code practice (Terraform, OpenTofu, Pulumi, or AWS CDK) as the authoritative source of environment configuration

- Comfortable operating in a regulated, security-conscious environment where architecture decisions have compliance implications

- Familiarity with AWS cost structure, along with the ability to factor in cost-related considerations when designing infrastructure

- Professional English; Dutch is a plus

Nice to have: 

- Experience specifically with observability/logging platforms at scale (e.g. OpenSearch, Grafana/Loki stacks, or equivalent) — bringing an implementation to production-hardened state, not just standing it up

- Experience in medical device, healthcare, or another regulated industry

- Familiarity with multi-tenant, per-customer cloud architectures (e.g. isolated accounts or workloads per client/region)

- Experience in a startup or scale-up environment

How We Work 

At Vitestro, ownership is not a slogan - it is an expectation. We trust people to take responsibility, make decisions, and drive work forward.

We believe breakthroughs happen when talented people combine dedication, accountability, and teamwork. That means:

- We take initiative rather than wait for direction.

- We focus on execution and delivering results.

- We proactively remove blockers and help each other succeed.

- We challenge ideas, not people.

- We continuously learn, improve, and raise the bar.

- We celebrate team success over individual heroics.

We move fast, but we do so thoughtfully. We care deeply about quality because the technology we build ultimately impacts patients and healthcare professionals.

If you are looking for an environment where you can make a significant contribution, take ownership of meaningful work, and be surrounded by highly motivated colleagues, we'd love to meet you.

What we offer 

- Competitive salary including a pension plan

- 25 days of annual leave (full-time position)

- A high-skilled team based in Utrecht

- Frequent out-of-work team activities and an annual company weekend away

- A training budget

- The chance to help shape the new niche of autonomous medical robotics

We’re big fans of working from the office – this is where team spirit comes alive. At the same time, we offer flexibility, allowing up to two (out of 5) days of working from home for those who prefer it. 

Are you excited? 

We totally understand that and so are we! By joining us, you can play an active role in changing the future of health care. Excited to join our revolution? Then we’d love to hear from you! 

If you think you've got what it takes, but you don't meet all the requirements - we still recommend you apply. We would love to learn about your interest and experience and consider if you can be a good fit for Vitestro. Nobody is a perfect fit, and we welcome applications with imperfections. We offer a learning environment where we grow together!

title: Senior Software Engineer – AI, Data & Product (m/w/d)
description:
Das Betriebssystem für die digitale Hausverwaltung

nu estate entwickelt ein KI-natives Betriebssystem für die Immobilienverwaltung in Hamburg und Umgebung. Das Ziel ist eine digitale Hausverwaltung für Eigentümer, die Transparenz, Qualität und Effizienz verbindet. Technologie und operative Bewirtschaftung werden zusammengedacht, um Anliegen von Eigentümern, Mietern und Dienstleistern zuverlässiger zu bearbeiten und eine belastbare Datenbasis für die Bewirtschaftung aufzubauen.

Du möchtest nicht nur Funktionen entwickeln, sondern verstehen, welches Problem sie im Alltag lösen? Bei nu estate verbindest du Softwareentwicklung, KI und Immobilienpraxis. Du baust an einem Produkt, das Informationen aus bestehenden Unterlagen nutzbar macht, operative Abläufe vereinfacht und verlässliche Entscheidungen ermöglicht.

Deine Rolle

Als Senior Software Engineer übernimmst du technische Verantwortung für wesentliche Teile unseres Produkts. Dein Schwerpunkt liegt auf Backend, Daten und KI-gestützten Abläufen. Du begleitest Lösungen vom Verständnis des fachlichen Problems über Datenmodell und Implementierung bis zum verlässlichen Betrieb.

Ein zentraler Teil deiner Arbeit ist, mit uns ein KI-natives ERP für die Immobilienverwaltung der nächsten Generation zu bauen. Du entwickelst die Produkt- und Datenarchitektur, die Informationen aus Mietverträgen, Objektunterlagen, Tabellen und PDFs in eine verlässliche Grundlage für Prozesse und Entscheidungen verwandelt. Darauf aufbauend gestaltest du intelligente Workflows, Automatisierungen und Integrationen, die operative Abläufe nicht nur abbilden, sondern grundlegend vereinfachen. So entsteht Schritt für Schritt ein System, in dem Daten, KI und tägliche Arbeit nahtlos zusammenwirken – von der Erfassung bis zur fundierten Entscheidung.

Das sind deine Aufgaben

- Am Kernprodukt bauen: Du entwickelst Datenmodelle, Backend-Dienste und APIs für Immobilien, Mietverhältnisse und operative Vorgänge. Wenn eine Lösung auch Änderungen an der Oberfläche braucht, denkst du diese mit.

- LLM-Pipelines produktionsreif machen: Du entwickelst die Dokumentenverarbeitung von der Extraktion bis zum validierten Import. Du berücksichtigst uneinheitliche Unterlagen, widersprüchliche Angaben, Mehrfachverarbeitung und notwendige manuelle Prüfungen.

- Manuelle Arbeit reduzieren: Gemeinsam mit dem operativen Team identifizierst du Engpässe und setzt passende Automatisierungen und Integrationen um. Du entscheidest bewusst, wo KI sinnvoll ist und wo klare Regeln die bessere Lösung sind.

- Eine verlässliche Datenbasis schaffen: Du sorgst für konsistente Daten und nachvollziehbare Kennzahlen und entwickelst Auswertungen, die konkrete Fragen zur Bewirtschaftung beantworten.

- Verantwortung im Betrieb übernehmen: Du machst Qualität und Fehler sichtbar, entwickelst Tests und Evaluationen und achtest auf Sicherheit, Wartbarkeit und Kosten.

- Technische Qualität im Team stärken: Du bringst dich in Architekturentscheidungen ein, gibst konstruktives Feedback und unterstützt weniger erfahrene Kolleg:innen dabei, gute Lösungen zu entwickeln.

Das bringst du mit

- Du hast mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Softwareentwicklung und bereits relevante Teile einer Anwendung selbstständig entwickelt und produktiv betreut.

- Du bist im Backend zu Hause und sicher im Umgang mit relationalen Datenbanken, SQL, APIs und sauber strukturiertem Code.

- Du hast praktische Erfahrung mit LLM-Anwendungen oder KI-gestützter Datenverarbeitung. Du weißt, dass eine überzeugende Demonstration noch keine belastbare Lösung ist.

- Du arbeitest KI-nativ: Du nutzt KI-Werkzeuge selbstverständlich, kannst ihre Ergebnisse fachlich beurteilen und verlässt dich bei Qualität und Architektur nicht auf ungeprüfte Vorschläge.

- Du denkst vom Problem her, triffst pragmatische technische Entscheidungen und bringst Aufgaben zuverlässig zu einem nutzbaren Ergebnis.

- Du kommunizierst klar, sprichst Risiken früh an und gehst offen mit Feedback um.

- Du möchtest verstehen, wie Immobilien bewirtschaftet werden und welche Auswirkungen technische Entscheidungen auf Eigentümer:innen, Mieter:innen und das operative Team haben.

Zusätzliche Pluspunkte: Besonders wertvoll ist Berufserfahrung im ERP-Umfeld, in der Versorgungswirtschaft oder Abrechnung sowie in der Immobilien- bzw. Hausverwaltung. Auch Erfahrung mit Dokumentenextraktion, Datenmigrationen, BI, Cloud-Betrieb oder der Entwicklung von Weboberflächen ist hilfreich. Du musst nicht in jedem Bereich Expert:in sein. Entscheidend sind technische Tiefe, Lernfähigkeit und die Bereitschaft, Verantwortung zu übernehmen.

Was die Arbeit bei uns ausmacht

- Verantwortung mit Gestaltungsspielraum: Du bringst dich in technische und produktbezogene Entscheidungen ein und begleitest deine Lösungen bis in die Anwendung.

- Nähe zur Immobilienpraxis: Fachliche Anforderungen entstehen aus konkreten Abläufen. Du arbeitest mit dem operativen Team daran, was tatsächlich verbessert werden muss.

- Tempo mit Qualitätsanspruch: Wir wollen früh nutzbare Ergebnisse sehen und daraus lernen. Verlässlichkeit, nachvollziehbare Daten und sorgfältiger Umgang mit sensiblen Informationen gehören dazu.

- Offenheit und Verbindlichkeit: Wir geben ehrliches Feedback, sprechen Probleme direkt an und halten Zusagen ein. Respekt und Zusammenarbeit auf Augenhöhe sind uns wichtig.

- Neugier und Kundennutzen: Gute Argumente und Daten zählen mehr als die eigene Lieblingslösung. Erfolg bedeutet für uns, dass die Arbeit für die Menschen hinter den Prozessen besser wird.

Interesse?

Wir freuen uns auf deinen Lebenslauf und eine kurze Vorstellung eines Systems oder Produkts, für das du technische Verantwortung übernommen hast. Was war das Problem, welche Entscheidungen hast du getroffen und woran hast du erkannt, dass die Lösung funktioniert? Besonders interessiert uns, wie du KI eingesetzt und ihre Ergebnisse überprüft hast.

Vergütung

Das Jahresgehalt liegt bei EUR 75,000–95,000.

description:

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

Nebius Token Factory is looking for scientists who can turn frontier LLM and VLM inference bottlenecks into research questions, conduct rigorous experiments, and translate their findings into production capabilities. AIM Solutions is an early-stage deep-tech startup in Eindhoven building inspection and metrology equipment for the semiconductor industry. We are in an active build phase, small, and growing.

You own how our tool is controlled and operated. The machine combines lasers, high-speed cameras, a nanometer-precision wafer stage and GPU-based image reconstruction. Every measurement depends on these parts working together in tight synchronization. You are the system engineer for that layer: the control architecture, the timing, the machine software, and the data path from sensor to result. You work side by side with our system engineer for the metrology hardware and with our algorithms team, and together you lead the system.

You will:

- Own the system control architecture: machine software, control hardware, timing and synchronization, and the data path from acquisition to reconstruction

- Translate system performance and throughput goals into requirements for control, software and compute, and keep them traceable

- Own the timing, throughput and data budgets, and decide where time is won or lost in a measurement

- Define and guard the interfaces between control software, hardware and algorithms, including the hardware abstraction layer

- Define how the machine is operated: machine states, sequencing, recipes, error handling, logging and monitoring

- Steer the software and embedded engineers on the control side: set priorities, run design reviews and resolve trade-offs

- Set up integration and verification of the control layer, with a test strategy that keeps it reliable as the hardware changes between builds

- Carry the machine software from lab prototype toward a production tool that runs unattended in a fab

Your profile 

- 8+ years in high-tech equipment, including several years as a system engineer, software architect or control architect for a complex machine

- Experience with machine control in semiconductor, lithography, metrology or scientific instruments

- Hands-on understanding of real-time and deterministic systems: hardware triggering, FPGA-based synchronization, motion control and high-rate data acquisition

- Strong in equipment software architecture: layered designs, hardware abstraction, state machines and concurrency

- Comfortable reading code and reviewing designs in Python and C/C++. You won’t write most of the code, but you can.

- Strong in requirements, budgets and interface management across hardware and software

- This is not a role in a large organization with fixed processes: you help decide how we work. You thrive in a small, fast-moving team where roles are fluid, and you are as likely to be at the lab bench debugging a trigger as in a design review.

- A clear communicator with engineers, management and partners

Bonus:

- Taking machine software from prototype to production, including SEMI standards for equipment communication and automation (such as SECS/GEM) and machine safety

- Integration with wafer handling and factory automation

- High-throughput data pipelines or GPU computing

- Experience with optical or imaging systems: cameras, lasers, image data

- Model-based systems engineering or modern requirements tools

We care more about systems thinking and ownership than about a perfect match. If your title was software architect, control architect or lead engineer, but you have owned how a complex machine runs, apply anyway.

title: CDI - Context & Analytics Engineer Manager - Paris
description:
Mission 

Un agent ne vaut que ce que valent les données et les connaissances sur lesquelles il répond. Pipelines, modèles de données, définitions de métriques, droits d’accès : vous créez et gouvernez ce socle, et les applications et les agents de nos clients s’appuient dessus. Quand un analyste ou un agent demande un chiffre, la réponse est celle de l’équipe finance, accompagnée de sa définition et de sa source.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez que les métiers et les agents puissent se fier aux données, et les utilisent. 

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype Context & Analytics Engineer.

Activités et responsabilités 

Avec les équipes métier et les analystes, il s’agit de définir ce que signifie chaque métrique et de vérifier que les données y correspondent. Sur ce socle, les Product Engineers et les AI Engineers construisent applications et agents.

Les Platform Engineers exploitent l’infrastructure sur laquelle tournent vos pipelines. Les échanges avec les data owners et les équipes de gouvernance du client, la relecture de code entre pairs et l’accompagnement des nouvelles recrues complètent le quotidien.

Vos responsabilités : 

- Construire des pipelines d’ingestion et des modèles de données, avec dbt par exemple.

- Mettre en place des contrôles de qualité des données et maintenir le lineage.

- Construire la couche sémantique et les définitions de métriques, pour que les personnes et les agents utilisent les mêmes chiffres, y compris en text-to-SQL.

- Définir les règles de gouvernance et les droits d’accès.

- Construire des pipelines de connaissances pour le RAG : indexation, chunking, métadonnées, permissions.

- Préparer le contexte exploitable par les agents : métadonnées, définitions, lineage et permissions.

Profil recherché 

Les indispensables : 

- Vous écrivez du SQL avec aisance et modélisez les données pour l’analyse.

- Des pipelines de données planifiés, testés et surveillés figurent à votre actif.

- Aux côtés des équipes métier, vous définissez les métriques et vérifiez que les données veulent bien dire ce que tout le monde croit y lire.

- La qualité des données, la documentation et les droits d’accès comptent pour vous.

- Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.

Un plus, pas un prérequis : 

- Python pour le traitement de données.

- Une plateforme de données cloud, comme BigQuery, Snowflake ou Databricks.

- Une couche sémantique ou un metrics store.

- La préparation de documents pour le RAG : chunking, indexation, métadonnées.

- Des outils de data catalogue ou de lineage.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? 

Dans un métier où deux tableaux de bord affichent parfois deux chiffres différents, ce poste consiste à rétablir la confiance : un chiffre juste, une définition partagée, une source identifiable. Ce travail, discret quand il réussit, conditionne tout ce que les autres archétypes construisent au-dessus.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’apprend sur les projets, avec les AI Engineers et l’appui de la communauté Context & Analytics Engineer, notamment le context engineering, c’est-à-dire le travail qui rend les données exploitables par les agents d’IA. À partir de 2027, l’archétype Context & Analytics Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (évaluation de l’IA, responsabilité en production).

Plus tard, un rôle transverse devient possible (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), tout comme les chapters AI Architect et AI Product Manager.

Processus de recrutement 

Le processus demande environ quatre heures, réparties en six étapes dont une seule sur site.

- Entretien RH (45 min, à distance) : parcours, motivations et points pratiques, comme le calendrier et les prétentions salariales.

- Appel avec le CTO (15 à 30 min, à distance).

- Screening technique (30 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter AI Applied Engineer) : retour détaillé sur vos projets passés, puis questions techniques et de design de solution.

- Code review et live coding (60 min, sur site, avec un membre du chapter) : relecture d’un dépôt de code existant et correction de ses défauts, puis construction d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité avec un coding agent et présentation du résultat.

- Cas technique (45 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter) : cadrage d’un problème métier, proposition d’une solution technique, description de la méthode d’évaluation, puis discussion de vos choix.

- Entretien final (30 min, à distance, avec une personne de l’encadrement du département, Engineering Manager ou Director) : reprise des points restés ouverts, choix de l’archétype et du niveau les mieux adaptés à votre profil, et réponses à toutes vos questions.

title: CDI - Context & Analytics Engineer Manager - Paris
description:
Mission 

Un agent ne vaut que ce que valent les données et les connaissances sur lesquelles il répond. Pipelines, modèles de données, définitions de métriques, droits d’accès : vous créez et gouvernez ce socle, et les applications et les agents de nos clients s’appuient dessus. Quand un analyste ou un agent demande un chiffre, la réponse est celle de l’équipe finance, accompagnée de sa définition et de sa source.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez que les métiers et les agents puissent se fier aux données, et les utilisent. 

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype Context & Analytics Engineer.

Activités et responsabilités 

Avec les équipes métier et les analystes, il s’agit de définir ce que signifie chaque métrique et de vérifier que les données y correspondent. Sur ce socle, les Product Engineers et les AI Engineers construisent applications et agents.

Les Platform Engineers exploitent l’infrastructure sur laquelle tournent vos pipelines. Les échanges avec les data owners et les équipes de gouvernance du client, la relecture de code entre pairs et l’accompagnement des nouvelles recrues complètent le quotidien.

Vos responsabilités : 

- Construire des pipelines d’ingestion et des modèles de données, avec dbt par exemple.

- Mettre en place des contrôles de qualité des données et maintenir le lineage.

- Construire la couche sémantique et les définitions de métriques, pour que les personnes et les agents utilisent les mêmes chiffres, y compris en text-to-SQL.

- Définir les règles de gouvernance et les droits d’accès.

- Construire des pipelines de connaissances pour le RAG : indexation, chunking, métadonnées, permissions.

- Préparer le contexte exploitable par les agents : métadonnées, définitions, lineage et permissions.

Profil recherché 

Les indispensables : 

- Vous écrivez du SQL avec aisance et modélisez les données pour l’analyse.

- Des pipelines de données planifiés, testés et surveillés figurent à votre actif.

- Aux côtés des équipes métier, vous définissez les métriques et vérifiez que les données veulent bien dire ce que tout le monde croit y lire.

- La qualité des données, la documentation et les droits d’accès comptent pour vous.

- Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.

Un plus, pas un prérequis : 

- Python pour le traitement de données.

- Une plateforme de données cloud, comme BigQuery, Snowflake ou Databricks.

- Une couche sémantique ou un metrics store.

- La préparation de documents pour le RAG : chunking, indexation, métadonnées.

- Des outils de data catalogue ou de lineage.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? 

Dans un métier où deux tableaux de bord affichent parfois deux chiffres différents, ce poste consiste à rétablir la confiance : un chiffre juste, une définition partagée, une source identifiable. Ce travail, discret quand il réussit, conditionne tout ce que les autres archétypes construisent au-dessus.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’apprend sur les projets, avec les AI Engineers et l’appui de la communauté Context & Analytics Engineer, notamment le context engineering, c’est-à-dire le travail qui rend les données exploitables par les agents d’IA. À partir de 2027, l’archétype Context & Analytics Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (évaluation de l’IA, responsabilité en production).

Plus tard, un rôle transverse devient possible (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), tout comme les chapters AI Architect et AI Product Manager.

Processus de recrutement 

Le processus demande environ quatre heures, réparties en six étapes dont une seule sur site.

- Entretien RH (45 min, à distance) : parcours, motivations et points pratiques, comme le calendrier et les prétentions salariales.

- Appel avec le CTO (15 à 30 min, à distance).

- Screening technique (30 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter AI Applied Engineer) : retour détaillé sur vos projets passés, puis questions techniques et de design de solution.

- Code review et live coding (60 min, sur site, avec un membre du chapter) : relecture d’un dépôt de code existant et correction de ses défauts, puis construction d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité avec un coding agent et présentation du résultat.

- Cas technique (45 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter) : cadrage d’un problème métier, proposition d’une solution technique, description de la méthode d’évaluation, puis discussion de vos choix.

- Entretien final (30 min, à distance, avec une personne de l’encadrement du département, Engineering Manager ou Director) : reprise des points restés ouverts, choix de l’archétype et du niveau les mieux adaptés à votre profil, et réponses à toutes vos questions.

Selon les étapes, tous les outils d’IA sont autorisés, ou aucun. Lors du live coding, c’est la manière de travailler avec l’assistance de l’IA qui est observée.

title: SIP Expert
description:
About ElevenLabs 

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

- 
ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

- 
ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

- 
ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

- 
High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

- 
Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

- 
AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

- 
Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

- 
Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

- 
Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

- 
Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

- 
Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

- 
Social travel : We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

- 
Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

- 
Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role 

We are looking for a SIP Expert to own the telephony layer that connects ElevenAgents voice agents to the phone network. SIP traffic is moving from early adoption to large enterprise call volumes, so the hard problems are now reliability and latency at scale.

Your general responsibilities will include: 

- 
Owning SIP end to end, from design doc to implementation, testing and ongoing operation, for a product used by enterprises at scale.

- 
Making call flows such as warm transfers dependable, and simplifying how our call services communicate with each other.

- 
Diagnosing and fixing load-related failures such as resource exhaustion and dropped connections.

- 
Collaborating with support, infrastructure and other teams to turn customer needs into shipped features.

Specific responsibilities might include: 

- 
Making our SIP edge and routing layer production-ready for large enterprise traffic.

- 
Designing and shipping lightweight, lower-latency call-handling services.

- 
Supporting carrier and SIP trunk integrations for enterprise customers.

You will join a small team of five, reporting directly to the team lead, with a high degree of ownership and very little bureaucracy.

Requirements 

We do not require any formal experience, certifications, or degrees. Instead, we are seeking enthusiastic engineers who can showcase solving impressively hard problems with artifacts such as past projects, designs, or open source contributions.

We do require: 

- 
Experience building and operating large-scale SIP/VoIP systems in production, including debugging load-related failures such as port exhaustion, dropped connections and state shared across services

- 
Hands-on experience running LiveKit (or comparable real-time media infrastructure) at scale, with comfort in WebSockets, WebRTC and RTP

- 
Strong backend engineering in Go or a comparable systems language, and a record of owning projects from design document through launch and maintenance

- 
Based in Europe or a nearby time zone, with at least 2 to 3 hours of daily overlap with CET

Bonus: Hands-on experience with Kamailio (or OpenSIPS/FreeSWITCH), or carrier and SIP trunk interconnects.

Location 

This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in Europe or nearby time zones, with the ability to operate in GMT to GMT+4 time zones preferred. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in Dublin, London and Warsaw.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

title: Control & Estimation Intern
description:
About Us 

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the Role 

We are developing the flight control systems of our next-generation autonomous platforms, which are embedded and subjected to extreme operational constraints. As with any aeronautical system, no model is perfect: aerodynamic effects, actuator dynamics, wind, payload changes, damage or degraded sensors are never fully captured by the physics-based models we rely on.

These unmodelled dynamics are one of the main sources of performance loss and risk for a controller, especially at the edge of the flight envelope. To push the boundaries of control, we are working on estimating these disturbances online and compensating for them in real time through adaptive control and robust estimation.

Your mission 

The goal of this internship is to design, implement and validate a framework for estimating and compensating unmodelled physics disturbances, in order to improve the robustness and performance of our flight controller in extreme and uncertain conditions.

Responsibilities 

- Literature review: Survey existing approaches to disturbance estimation and adaptive control

- Algorithm implementation: Develop and implement the selected estimation and compensation algorithms within our simulation environment.

- Performance evaluation: Assess and compare the performance and robustness of the developed methods against classical baselines.

- Embedded constraints: Ensure the solutions are compatible with real-time execution and the computational limits of onboard hardware.

- Documentation: Document all work performed, including methodologies, results and conclusions.

- Flight test participation: Actively take part in flight test sessions to validate the developed algorithms in operational conditions, and contribute to their real-time deployment.

Candidates Requirements 

- Educational background: Strong academic record in automatic control, applied mathematics, or a related field. Knowledge of state estimation (Kalman filtering, observers) and nonlinear or adaptive control is a strong plus.

- Technical skills : Solid understanding of control theory fundamentals and proficiency in Python or C++ is a plus. Experience with drones is a major plus.

- Mindset: You are curious to learn, autonomous, rigorous and able to take initiative.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

Der Hub verbindet Datenerfassung mittels Motion Capture, Physical-AI-Training und Multi-Robot-Benchmarking. Im Mittelpunkt stehen industrielle Use Cases unter industrienahen Bedingungen, darunter Materialtransport, das Be- und Entladen von Maschinen sowie die Automatisierung von Montageschritten.

Wir sind das INC Innovation Center , ein internationales Team, das produzierende Unternehmen dabei unterstützt neue Technologien zu erschließen und innovative Ideen in die Praxis umzusetzen.

Für den Aufbau und die Weiterentwicklung unseres Hubs suchen wir Menschen, die Lust haben, selbst anzupacken, technische Lösungen zu entwickeln und die Zukunft der Robotik aktiv mitzugestalten. 

Ihre Mission 

Sie bauen die technische Infrastruktur des Hubs auf und machen sie für unsere Anwendungs- und Technologiepartner sowie unser Entwicklungsteam nutzbar. Dabei verantworten Sie das Zusammenspiel von Robotik-Hardware und -Software, Sensorik, Greiftechnik, Datenpipelines und Automatisierungstechnik als integriertes Gesamtsystem.

Gemeinsam mit unserem Entwicklungsteam in Aachen und Stuttgart leiten Sie die technische Umsetzung industrieller Use Cases. Ihre Verantwortung reicht von der Anforderungsaufnahme über Architektur und Integration bis zur Inbetriebnahme, zum Benchmarking und zur Validierung.

Ein zentraler Fokus liegt auf Physical AI: Sie evaluieren und vergleichen aktuelle Foundation Models und Physical-AI-Modelle in verschiedenen Use-Case-Szenarien. Sie bereiten Modelle für konkrete industrielle Use Cases vor, passen sie durch anwendungsspezifisches Training/Fine-Tuning an und validieren ihre Leistungsfähigkeit in realen Robotik-Umgebungen.

Ihre Aufgaben

- Aufbau, Integration und Betrieb der technischen Infrastruktur für Datenerfassung, Modelltraining, Simulation und die Umsetzung realer Use Cases mit Robotik- und Physical-AI-Systemen. Dazu gehören unter anderem Sensorik, Greiftechnik, Motion-Capture-Equipment, Edge-Devices sowie Cloud- und Datenplattformen.

- Gemeinsame Ausgestaltung industrieller Use Cases mit Industriepartnern zur Erprobung mobiler und humanoider Roboter. Evaluation, Vergleich, Integration und Anpassung von Physical-AI-Modellen und Foundation Models für unterschiedliche Robotik-Hardwaresysteme. Durchführung von Machbarkeitsstudien, Benchmarks, Pilotprojekten und Validierungen unter industrienahen Bedingungen.

- Aufbau von Trainingsworkflows für das Erlernen von Bewegungsabläufen durch verschiedene humanoide Robotiksysteme. Die Workflows umfassen reale Datenerfassung/Data-Capturing-Pipelines (z.B. mittels Teleoperationssystemen), Simulation, Datenaugmentation, Modelltraining sowie die Übertragung auf physische Robotik-Hardware.

- Technische Leitung und Durchführung von Industrieprojekten im Hub gemeinsam mit dem technischen Team in Stuttgart und Aachen. Planung und Steuerung sprintorientierter Arbeitspakete entlang der gesamten Software- und Hardware-Toolchain. Koordination interner Teams, externer Technologiepartner und industrieller Kunden.

- Entwicklung der technischen Roadmap sowie Identifikation neuer Technologien, Partner und Anwendungsfelder. Beratung von Industriepartnern sowie industriellen Kunden bei der technischen Vorbereitung, Umsetzung und Bewertung ihrer Robotik- und Physical-AI-Use-Cases.

Ihr Profil

- Abgeschlossenes Diplom- oder Masterstudium in Robotik, Mechatronik, Elektrotechnik, Informatik, Maschinenbau, Automatisierungstechnik, Künstlicher Intelligenz oder einem vergleichbaren technischen Bereich. Promotion ist wünschenswert, jedoch keine Voraussetzung.

- Mindestens 3 Jahre Berufserfahrung im Robotikumfeld; idealerweise bringen Sie mehr als fünf Jahre Erfahrung mit. Besonders relevant sind Bezüge zu Robotik-Hardware, Robotik-Software, Automatisierung, Physical AI, Robot Learning, Sensorik, Simulation oder industriellen Anwendungsfällen.

- Erfahrung in der technischen Projektleitung komplexer Projekte mit internen und externen Partnern.

- Nachweisbare Erfahrung im Aufbau, in der Integration und im Betrieb von Robotik-Infrastruktur oder Automatisierungssystemen. Dazu gehören Kenntnisse über Robotik-Hardware verschiedener Hersteller, Sensorik, Greiftechnik und Edge-Devices sowie über die Integration robotischer Gesamtsysteme.

- Grundlegende Erfahrung mit ROS 2, Python und Linux sowie mit Simulationstools wie NVIDIA Isaac Sim/Lab oder MuJoCo beziehungsweise vergleichbaren Technologien.

- Wünschenswert sind Erfahrungen mit Physical AI und Foundation Models, insbesondere VLA-Modellen, sowie mit robotischen Lernverfahren wie Imitation Learning und Reinforcement Learning. Erfahrung im Fine-Tuning von KI-Modellen und im Aufbau von Data-Capturing-Pipelines ist ebenfalls von Vorteil.

- Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse.

Persönlichkeit und Arbeitsweise 

- Hohes Eigenengagement, unternehmerisches Denken und die Energie, neue Themen proaktiv voranzutreiben.

- Freude an einem dynamischen, sich schnell entwickelnden Umfeld und Bereitschaft, Verantwortung zu übernehmen.

- Schnelle Auffassungsgabe und Fähigkeit, sich eigenständig in neue Technologien und Fachgebiete einzuarbeiten.

- Offenheit für kontinuierliches Lernen, Experimentieren und Weiterentwicklung im Bereich Physical AI, Robot Learning und autonomer Robotik.

- Sie möchten Gestaltungsspielraum nutzen, mit dem Hub wachsen und seine Zukunft aktiv mitprägen. Dabei sind Sie Teil eines Teams mit großem Entwicklungspotenzial.

Was wir bieten

- Die Möglichkeit, einen hersteller- und technologieunabhängigen Physical-AI-Hub in Stuttgart von Beginn an aktiv mitzugestalten.

- Zugang zu mobiler und humanoider Robotik, Sensorik, Greiftechnik, Simulations- und KI-Infrastruktur.

- Ein internationales Netzwerk aus Industrieunternehmen, Technologiepartnern, Startups und Forschungseinrichtungen.

- Gestaltungsspielraum beim Aufbau und bei der Weiterentwicklung des Hubs: Sie prägen die technische Roadmap, das Team und die Partnerschaften mit.

- Die Stelle ist zunächst auf zwei Jahre befristet. Wir streben jedoch eine langfristige Zusammenarbeit an, sodass eine anschließende Entfristung ausdrücklich möglich ist.

Sie möchten den Future Robotics Exploration Hub aktiv mitgestalten? Dann freuen wir uns auf Ihren Lebenslauf und ein kurzes Motivationsschreiben.

title: Technical Marketing Engineer
description:
The role 

Neural Concept is looking for a Technical Marketing Engineer to turn emerging engineering technologies into compelling demonstrations, technical content and joint partner stories.

You will explore how Neural Concept can work with technologies from partners, primarily NVIDIA, and prototype new engineering workflows. You will then translate that work into strong demos, videos and articles that make our technical depth tangible to the market.

Your content work will also extend beyond partner initiatives. You will stay close to our Research, Frontier, Vertical Solutions and Product teams to understand what they are building, identify stories worth taking to market and produce technical content independently. You will turn the work into a technically credible article explaining the method, findings and implications.

This role sits within Marketing and works closely with Product Marketing, Partner Marketing, Research, Product, Engineering and our Vertical Solutions teams.

Your mission 

Make Neural Concept’s technical capabilities visible and understandable.

You will combine hands-on engineering work with strong market judgement. You will start with the audience and the story we want to tell, then build the right prototype or content to prove it.

The goal is to create credible and visually strong demonstrations of what becomes possible when Neural Concept connects with emerging AI and engineering technologies. These are marketing prototypes, not production-ready integrations. They must communicate the concept clearly and remain technically accurate.

What you will do 

Drive technical co-builds with partners 

- Explore partner technologies and identify where they can create new engineering workflows with Neural Concept.

- Lead technical co-build initiatives, with an initial focus on the NVIDIA ecosystem, including technologies such as PhysicsNeMo, Warp, Omniverse and agentic frameworks.

- Build prototypes that combine Neural Concept capabilities with partner products and infrastructure.

- Work directly with partner technical and marketing teams to shape joint stories.

- Turn technical exploration into demos, videos, event content and other co-marketing assets.

- Identify new opportunities for joint content, launches and market visibility.

Produce technical marketing content 

- Write technically grounded articles, explainers and demo narratives.

- Create and present demos for partners, events, campaigns and executive conversations.

- Develop demo scripts and work with design or video specialists to produce polished assets.

- Repackage internal prototypes and engineering work into content that external audiences can understand and remember.

- Help Product and Partner Marketing communicate technical mechanisms precisely, without unnecessary complexity.

Build for the audience 

- Define the audience, message and desired outcome before starting technical work.

- Make deliberate choices about what needs to work end to end and what can remain a prototype.

- Prioritise a clear story, strong visual execution and market relevance.

- Simplify the experience without oversimplifying the technology.

- Validate technical claims with the relevant internal experts before publication.

What we are looking for 

- A strong engineering background

- The ability to build technical prototypes independently. Experience with Python and AI or engineering software is strongly preferred.

- Knowledge of one or more relevant areas: machine learning, physics AI, simulation, CAD/CAE, geometry processing, engineering software or agentic systems.

- Evidence that you can explain technical subjects through writing, demos or video.

- A marketing-first mindset. You think about the audience and the intended reaction, not only the technical implementation.

- Strong visual and product judgement. You care about how a demo looks and how clearly it communicates value.

- Comfort working with external technology partners and coordinating across technical and marketing teams.

- The ability to move quickly through ambiguity and build enough to prove a concept.

- Excellent written and spoken English.

This role may suit you if 

- You are an engineer who has repeatedly moved towards storytelling, demos, content or developer marketing.

- You enjoy experimenting with new technologies and immediately think about how to show their value.

- You want to influence how a deep-tech company presents its capabilities to the market.

- You prefer building a convincing prototype and narrative over maintaining production systems.

- You can challenge a technically impressive idea when it does not serve the audience or the message.

This role is probably not for you if 

- Your primary interest is delivering reliable customer implementations or maintaining production integrations.

- You optimise technical work without considering how an external audience will understand it.

- You see writing, storytelling and visual presentation as tasks to hand over after the engineering work is complete.

- You are uncomfortable making pragmatic trade-offs when building exploratory prototypes.

How the role complements Product Marketing 

Our Product and Technology Marketing function owns the broader product narrative, positioning and business value. The Technical Marketing Engineer brings deeper hands-on engineering capacity.

The two roles work together: Product Marketing defines the story and market context; the Technical Marketing Engineer explores the technology, builds the proof and contributes the technical content.

What success looks like 

Within the first year, you will have:

- Established a repeatable technical co-build motion with NVIDIA and other priority partners.

- Produced partner demonstrations that create concrete content, event and relationship opportunities.

- Built a steady flow of high-quality technical articles, demos and videos.

- Made complex Neural Concept capabilities easier to understand without weakening their technical substance.

- Become the bridge between Marketing, Engineering and partner technical teams.

We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and we're committed to building a diverse and inclusive environment where you can thrive.

title: Head of Software
description:
We can't hire everyone… but we can help them shine somewhere brilliant. 

At Octopus, we're lucky to attract some incredibly talented humans. And while we can’t bring every talented person into our team, we can help them land somewhere that’s just as mission-driven. That’s why we’re sharing opportunities from MOPO; a company we’ve proudly backed through a strategic investment. 

MOPO is on a mission to enable renewable energy access in underserved markets. Already operating in Nigeria, DRC, Sierra Leone and Liberia, our solar power stations distribute energy through proprietary MOPO batteries managed by a network of local agents. Our model is already powering thousands of homes and small businesses, reducing reliance on fossil fuels and enabling livelihoods. With backing from Octopus Energy, British International Investment, and Norfund, MOPO is scaling rapidly and is positioned to transform energy access and e-mobility across the continent. 

Joining our growing team, you’ll provide hands-on technical leadership and people management for the software team behind MOPO’s core software products: our Android Rental App and the MOPO Platform, a web application built with Django, Python and Vue.js. Together, these tools enable our network of local agents to manage battery distribution and customer relationships across our markets. 

You’ll manage four engineers, two platform engineers and two mobile app engineers, helping them develop their skills, solve challenging problems and deliver reliable software. We have been steadily growing our team and this expansion is likely to continue. Working closely with product managers and stakeholders across the business, you’ll connect engineering decisions to the needs of our agents, customers and operations teams. 

You’ll own and develop our engineering ways of working. We currently use an Agile/Kanban approach, and we’re looking for someone who can build on that foundation as we grow: improving how we plan, collaborate and deliver, while keeping processes practical and proportionate to the team. 

We’re a small, growing team supporting an expanding product range across multiple markets in Sub-Saharan Africa. Things move quickly, so you’ll need the flexibility and pragmatism to keep delivery moving, alongside the judgement and confidence to challenge priorities and push back on unrealistic expectations. 

Working location 

The role is based primarily in our Sheffield HQ, with up to two days working from home if desired. Occasional international travel to Sub-Saharan Africa is entirely optional, but is something they offer to all of their employees if they are interested. 

The role will interest you if... 

- 
You’re excited by building technology that improves access to clean energy and supports local entrepreneurs across Africa. 

- 
You enjoy helping engineers grow, giving clear direction and creating an environment where people can do their best work. 

- 
You’re keen to stay hands-on. Your primary focus will be ensuring that the team is working effectively, but you should also expect to write some code! 

- 
You want to stay close to technology while taking responsibility for the team’s development, technical direction and delivery. 

- 
You enjoy improving how a team works and adapting your approach as its needs change 

On a given day you'll likely... 

- 
Work with product managers and stakeholders to turn business and user needs into clear, achievable engineering priorities. 

- 
Help the team break down work, identify dependencies and risks, and communicate progress and trade-offs. 

- 
Guide technical decisions across our mobile applications and platform, balancing immediate needs with reliability, maintainability and future growth. 

- 
Write some code, review some PRs. 

- 
Champion thoughtful testing, code review and release practices that help the team deliver confidently. 

- 
Develop our Agile/Kanban ways of working, addressing bottlenecks and helping the team make continuous improvements. 

- 
Help the team investigate issues from the field and turn what we learn into lasting improvements. 

- 
Work with leadership to shape the team’s capabilities and hiring needs as MOPO grows. 

- 
Support and develop your engineers through regular one-to-ones, coaching, feedback and career development conversations 

We would like to hear from you if you have the following experience... 

- 
Leading or managing software engineers, with experience coaching people, providing constructive feedback and supporting their development. 

- 
A strong software engineering background and the technical judgement to guide architecture, review proposals and help engineers work through complex problems. 

- 
Working closely with product managers and stakeholders to prioritise work and deliver useful software. 

- 
Using Agile or Kanban approaches in practice, and improving team processes based on what the team needs. 

- 
Taking responsibility for software quality, reliability and maintainability throughout the development lifecycle. 

- 
Communicating technical choices and delivery trade-offs clearly to technical and non-technical colleagues. 

Ideally, your engineering background will include Django/Python or mobile application development with Android or iOS. However, we’re flexible on software stack: sound engineering judgement, effective leadership and a willingness to learn matter more than familiarity with every technology we use. 

More about MOPO: 

MOPO is on a mission to enable renewable energy access in underserved markets. Already operating in Nigeria, DRC, Sierra Leone and Liberia, our solar power stations distribute energy through proprietary MOPO Batteries managed by a network of local agents. 

Our model is already powering thousands of homes and small businesses - eliminating fossil fuel use and enabling livelihoods. 

With backing from Octopus Energy, British International Investment, and Norfund, MOPO is scaling rapidly and is positioned to transform energy access and e-mobility across the continent

title: Cryogenics Engineer – Test Facility & Auxiliary Cryoplants
description:
WHO WE ARE 

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO 

- Shape the architecture of the world’s first commercial fusion power plant – Own system-level decisions that determine how a first-of-a-kind energy technology is designed, integrated, and ultimately deployed at scale.

- Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges – Work across tightly coupled disciplines (plasma physics, magnets, cryogenics, manufacturing, controls, and more) to resolve critical trade-offs and turn cutting-edge science into a functioning product.

- Design real hardware with a pragmatic, fast-moving team from all over the world – Combine advanced simulation and systems thinking with a strong execution mindset, focusing on practical engineering solutions that accelerate the path to commercial fusion energy.

YOUR IMPACT 

You will deliver the helium refrigerator and cryogenic distribution for Proxima's Alpha coil test facility, taking these systems from requirements and process design through procurement, installation and commissioning. You will also support the engineering of the refrigerator for the cryopumps of the neutral beam injectors and divertor, and act as the process and safety owner for these systems.

WHAT YOU WILL DO 

- Own the cryogenic supply infrastructure for the Alpha coil test facility, covering the main refrigerator, liquid nitrogen equipment, cryogenic distribution and interconnecting valve box, from concept to commissioning and test operation

- Define requirements, process flow diagrams and P&IDs for cryogenic refrigerators and ancillary systems such as helium storage tanks, LHe dewars, purification and gas recovery

- Size lines, valves and pressure relief devices based on your relief case definitions, in line with PED and relevant EN/ISO standards

- Write specifications and RFQ packages, evaluate offers, and act as expert customer for suppliers through design reviews, FAT, installation and site acceptance

- Plan and lead installation and commissioning, write operating procedures, and support operation on site close to Munich

WHO YOU ARE 

- A team player who loves challenges and is not afraid to experiment, take risks and learn from mistakes

- A proven track record of designing, building and commissioning cryogenic or similar gas systems in industrial plants, test facilities, accelerators, or space infrastructure

- Hands-on experience developing P&IDs, sizing pressure relief devices to recognised standards (e.g. ISO 21013, ISO 4126), and using process or system simulation tools such as EcosimPro or Aspen HYSYS for helium refrigeration plants or similar

- Experience with pressure equipment design to EN 13445 or AD 2000, and with CAD

- Proficiency with programming languages used in science and engineering (particularly Python) is highly beneficial but not essential

- Demonstrated ability to manage the delivery of complex systems with external suppliers to schedule and budget

INTERVIEW PROCESS 

- Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

- Technical Screening (30 min)

- Technical Panel (3x60 min)

- CEO call (30 min)

This role sits at L2/L3/L4 of our framework, please inquire during the recruitment process for further information 

At Proxima Fusion, our mission is bold: making limitless clean energy a reality. To get there, we need a high-performing, diverse team that brings different perspectives, challenges assumptions, and builds together with purpose. We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. We don't look at how you identify, what you look like, who you choose to worship or what ethnicity you are. We care about what you can bring to the table.

title: Thermo-Mechanical Engineer
description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecraft for humanity.

The heart of a spacecraft lies in its engines, and that's why we, at The Exploration Company, are dedicated to developing our own cutting-edge Propulsion Systems ensuring the highest level of efficiency and reliability in our space endeavours.

We are seeking a talented Thermo-Mechanical Engineer to join our Future Project division. As a key member of our engineering team, you will be responsible for designing, analyzing, and optimizing combustion devices for cryogenic rocket engines, with a focus on the main thrust chamber assembly.

Key Responsibilities

- Support structural and thermal analysis of combustion device hardware including injector heads, faceplates, combustion chambers, manifolds, and structural interfaces.

- Perform finite element analysis (FEA) and establish practical design suggestions and establish design recommendations, and margin assessments for hardware development.

- Develop and apply analytical and reduced-order models to estimate heat transfer, structural loads, and thermal boundary conditions to inform design trades and hardware maturation.

- Support hardware development and maturation, including design iteration, development planning, test definition, and post-test assessment of structural and thermal performance.

- Drive life assessment activities, including low-cycle fatigue, thermal fatigue, cyclic loading, margin tracking, and damage accumulation for reusable hardware.

- Own structural reliability and lifecycle assessments of combustion hardware, including low-cycle fatigue, thermal fatigue, cyclic loading, and thermo-mechanical failure risk evaluation.

- Collaborate with combustion and fluid engineers to translate predicted heat flux distributions, pressure fields, and flow characteristics into structural and thermal design requirements

- Define structural and thermal instrumentation strategies for development testing and participate post-test data reduction, model validation, and correlation activities.

- Contribute to material selection and design trades considering temperature capability, strength, fatigue resistance, oxidation compatibility, and cryogenic behavior.

- Prepare technical documentation and contribute to design, and test reviews with clear technical justification and risk assessment.

What we would love to see from you

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

- Experience (academic, internship, or professional) in structural or thermal analysis of high-performance mechanical systems.

- Strong fundamentals in solid mechanics, heat transfer, and pressure-loaded structures.

- Experience with FEA tools such as ANSYS, NASTRAN, Abaqus, or equivalent.

- Ability to interpret complex thermal and pressure boundary conditions and apply them appropriately in structural models.

- Understanding of fatigue, temperature-dependent material behavior, and nonlinear structural response.

- Exposure to high-temperature or cryogenic systems is advantageous.

- Familiarity with CAD (NX ideally) tools and ability to work directly with geometry.

- Experience with Python or similar scripting tools for analysis automation or data processing is beneficial.

Skills and Behaviours 

- Methodical and structured approach to problem solving.

- Strong attention to detail and analytical rigor.

- Clear written and verbal communication of technical rationale.

- Ability to iterate analyses as design and test data evolve.

- Interest in propulsion systems and combustion device development.

- Demonstrates behaviors consistent with The Exploration Company’s core values of Mission, Vision, Integrity, Excellence, and Teamwork.

title: macOS & Jamf Automation Engineer
description:
We are looking for a hands-on macOS & Jamf Automation Engineer to engineer, automate and continuously improve the services that support our global Apple device estate. This role is focused on delivering a secure, reliable and consistent macOS experience at scale through Jamf Pro, reusable code, APIs and modern engineering practices. 

You will replace repetitive administration and one-off scripts with maintainable automation for device enrolment, configuration, application delivery, patching, compliance and lifecycle management. Working across Jamf Pro, Apple Business Manager, identity, security, asset and service-management platforms, you will build integrations and workflows that make Apple device services easier to operate, measure and support. 

Engineering mindset 
Automation is the product, not an afterthought. We are looking for someone who sees a manual Jamf task, fragile policy or recurring Mac support issue and asks, “How can we make this reliable, reusable and self-service?” 

You should be comfortable working from Apple and Jamf documentation, investigating unfamiliar behaviours and translating operational requirements into production-quality automation. Your solutions account for failure, test changes before release, scale to an enterprise environment, provide useful telemetry and favour reusable frameworks over isolated scripts. You take ownership from design through operation, document your work and balance long-term platform improvements with immediate business needs. 

What success looks like 
You will measurably reduce manual effort, deployment lead time and configuration drift across the macOS estate. Enrollment, configuration, software delivery, patching, security compliance and device lifecycle processes will become increasingly automated, observable, auditable and recoverable. 

Over time, you will establish a scalable Apple endpoint automation model based on Jamf Pro, APIs, version-controlled code, release pipelines and shared engineering standards rather than manual platform administration. 

What you'll do 

macOS Platform & Jamf Automation 

- 
Design and maintain automation for macOS enrolment, provisioning, configuration, application delivery, updates and device retirement using Jamf Pro. 

- 
Build reusable scripts, tools and workflows using shell scripting, Python, Jamf APIs and other appropriate technologies. 

- 
Administer and automate Jamf policies, configuration profiles, Jamf Blueprints, Jamf compliance, extension attributes, smart groups, packages and lifecycle workflows. 

- 
Integrate Jamf Pro and Apple Business Manager with identity, security, asset, infrastructure and service-management platforms. 

- 
Apply Git, CI/CD, automated testing and configuration-as-code practices so Apple platform changes are controlled, repeatable and auditable. 

Security, Compliance & Observability 

- 
Translate macOS security and compliance requirements into Jamf configuration profiles, automated controls and measurable outcomes. 

- 
Automate macOS and third-party application patching, vulnerability remediation and exception handling. 

- 
Build guardrails for FileVault, endpoint protection, authentication, privacy controls and device compliance. 

- 
Create inventory, telemetry, dashboards and alerting that provide actionable visibility into automation performance, Mac health and risk. 

- 
Partner with Security teams to automate evidence collection, audit reporting and remediation workflows for the Apple estate. 

Engineering, Lifecycle & Support 

- 
Define the macOS and Jamf automation architecture, engineering standards and roadmap for a global Apple device service. 

- 
Engineer automated packaging, deployment, update and rollback pipelines for macOS applications. 

- 
Evaluate Jamf, Apple and related ecosystem capabilities, APIs and emerging technologies to simplify or extend the service. 

- 
Troubleshoot complex failures across macOS, Jamf, identity, networking, security and application-delivery services. 

- 
Convert recurring Mac incidents and support escalations into automated detection, remediation or prevention. 

- 
Document designs, code, operating procedures and support models, and enable support teams to use them effectively. 

What you'll need 

- 
Jamf 300 certification. 

- 
4+ years of experience engineering and automating macOS services in a modern enterprise environment. 

- 
Deep hands-on expertise with Jamf Pro, including policies, profiles, smart groups, extension attributes, inventory, application deployment and API-based administration. 

- 
Strong knowledge of macOS management, Apple Business Manager, Automated Device Enrollment, declarative device management and Apple security controls. 

- 
Ability to build production-quality automation using shell scripting, Python, REST APIs and structured data formats, supported by Git, CI/CD, testing, secrets management, Jamf webhooks and code review. 

- 
Experience automating macOS application packaging, deployment, patching and vulnerability remediation; a bachelor’s degree in IT or Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience. 

Additional experience that would be valuable: 

- 
Experience with identity integrations, Platform SSO, certificate services, zero-touch deployment and device trust. 

- 
Knowledge of Installomator, swiftDialog, Nudge, or similar community and enterprise macOS automation tooling. 

- 
Experience integrating Jamf with ServiceNow, asset-management, security, observability or data platforms. 

- 
Cloud services, serverless functions, SQL or reporting technologies used to host integrations and analyse endpoint data. 

- 
Familiarity with Microsoft Intune, Linux or mobile device management in a broader endpoint environment. 

What we offer 

A competitive compensation package, of course. 

Time and resources to grow and develop, including a personal development budget and paid leave for learning days, as well as paid access to e-learning resources such as O’Reilly and LinkedIn Learning. 

Time to support life outside of work, with enhanced parental leave plus paid leave to care for loved ones and volunteer in local communities. 

Work flexibility, where TomTom’ers, in agreement with their manager and team, use both the office and home to focus, collaborate, learn and socialize. It’s all about getting the best out of both worlds – we ask TomTom’ers to come to the office two days a week, and the remaining three are free to be worked in either location.

Improve your home office with a setup budget and get extra support with a monthly allowance. 

Enjoy options to work from your home country and abroad for a set number of days each year, to visit family and friends, or to simply explore the world we’re mapping. 

Take the holidays you want with a competitive holiday plan, plus an extra day off to celebrate your birthday. 

Join annual events like our Hackathon and DevDays to bring your ideas to life with talented teammates from around the world. 

Become a part of our inclusive global culture and have the chance to collaborate with a diverse community – we have over 80 nationalities at TomTom! 

Find out more about our global benefits and enjoy additional local benefits tailored to your location. 

Meet your team 

We’re Employee IT. We’re on a mission to deliver a seamless user experience for TomTom'ers across. Whether we're creating solutions to enable collaboration, increase productivity or help people communicate, your work will ensure TomTom'ers are equipped to create the first real-time map. In our team, you’ll help design, develop, deliver, operate and support solutions through a defined set of services, so that we can continue to bring people closer to the world around them. 

At TomTom... 

You’ll help people find their way in the world. In 2004, TomTom revolutionized how the world moves with the introduction of the first portable navigation device. Now, we intend to do it again by engineering the first-ever real-time map, the smartest and most useful map on the planet.

Work with a team of 3,300+ unique, curious and passionate problem-solvers. Together, we’ll open up a world of possibilities for car manufacturers, enterprises and developers to help people understand and get closer to the world around them.

After you apply 

Our recruitment team will work hard to give you a meaningful experience throughout your journey with us, no matter the outcome. Your application will be screened closely and you can rest assured that all follow-up actions will be thorough, from assessments and interviews all the way through onboarding. To find out more about our application process, check out our hiring FAQs .

TomTom is an equal opportunity employer 

TomTom is where you can find your place in the world. Every day we welcome, nurture and celebrate differences. Why? Because your uniqueness is what makes you, you . No matter your culture or background, you’ll find your impact at TomTom. Research also shows that sometimes women and underrepresented communities can be hesitant to apply for positions unless they believe they meet 100% of the criteria. If you can relate to this, please know that we’d love to hear from you.

description:
Über nu estate

nu estate ist die digitale Hausverwaltung für Eigentümer mit hohem Anspruch an Transparenz, Qualität und Effizienz in Hamburg und Umgebung. Das Ziel ist der Aufbau eines KI-nativen Betriebssystems für die Immobilienverwaltung, das Technologie und operative Bewirtschaftung direkt verknüpft. Durch eine belastbare Datenbasis sollen Immobilien langfristig besser bewirtschaftet und fundierte Entscheidungen ermöglicht werden.

Das sind deine Aufgaben

In dieser Rolle unterstützen Sie die Produktentwicklung, den Bereich Business Intelligence und das Onboarding bei nu estate in Hamburg.

- Produktentwicklung: Anforderungen aus der Verwaltung und Bewirtschaftung von Immobilien verstehen, strukturieren und gemeinsam mit dem Team in Prototypen und Produktverbesserungen übersetzen.

Relevante Informationen extrahieren, auf das Zieldatenmodell abbilden, validieren und in unser System überführen. Quellen nachvollziehbar halten und unsichere Ergebnisse zur manuellen Prüfung kennzeichnen.

- KI-gestütztes Arbeiten: Wiederkehrende Aufgaben erkennen, geeignete KI-Werkzeuge einsetzen und einfache Automatisierungen erproben. Ergebnisse auf Richtigkeit, Nutzen und Datenschutz prüfen.

Das bringst du mit

- Du bist eingeschriebene:r Student:in, beispielsweise in Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik, Data Science oder einem vergleichbaren Studiengang.

- Du arbeitest KI-nativ: Du nutzt KI bereits regelmäßig zum Programmieren, Analysieren oder Erarbeiten von Lösungen. Du kannst erklären, was dein eigener Beitrag war und wie du die Ergebnisse überprüft hast.

- Du hast erste praktische Erfahrung mit Code, Daten oder Automatisierungen gesammelt – im Studium, in einem Nebenjob oder durch eigene Projekte.

- Du denkst strukturiert und wirst neugierig, wenn Informationen noch in unübersichtlichen Dokumenten oder manuellen Abläufen stecken.

- Du übernimmst Verantwortung für vereinbarte Aufgaben, sprichst Hindernisse früh an und gehst offen mit Feedback um.

- Du interessierst dich für Immobilien und möchtest die fachlichen Zusammenhänge hinter den Daten verstehen. Vorkenntnisse in der Immobilienwirtschaft sind kein Muss.

- Neugier statt Besserwisserei: Gute Argumente und Daten zählen mehr als die eigene Lieblingslösung. Wir wollen fachlich und menschlich dazulernen.

Vergütung

Die Vergütung für diese Werkstudentenstelle liegt bei EUR 15–20 pro Stunde.
